articles.title: The Global Story - How Lula held on to Brazil - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: A fierce election campaign ended in the defeat of another Bolsonaro.
articles.body:
World Service , · 27 Oct 2026 , · 27 mins

Brazil has just come through a fierce electoral campaign that saw left-wing incumbent Lula face Flavio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, the former president convicted of plotting a coup. Election night brought a series of unexpected turns before incumbent Lula Da Silva was declared the winner. Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the result and has called for the election to be annulled. But the result is significant: Brazil, Latin America’s largest democracy, has broken a trend that has seen right-wing candidates, many aligned with Donald Trump, win elections across the region. So what does a Lula victory mean for Latin America? In this episode, we speak to Nathalia Passarinho, an editor at BBC Brazil and BBC Mundo. articles.title: Benjamin Netanyahu’s life in pictures
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister in history.
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is in a tight race seen as a referendum on his leadership since the October 7, 2023, attacks .

He is facing off against Gadi Eisenkot , a former military chief

Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister in history.

He was sworn in for his sixth term in December 2022, 18 months after he was ousted from power.

Netanyahu became Israel's youngest-ever prime minister in 1996 and served until 1999. He led Israel's government again from 2009-2021.

articles.title: Homem de 42 anos morre após passar mal durante atividade física no Parque Ibirapuera, Zona Sul de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima teve um mal súbito e parou de respirar, segundo boletim de ocorrência. O óbito foi constatado no local.
articles.summary: Vítima teve um mal súbito e parou de respirar, segundo boletim de ocorrência. O óbito foi constatado no local.
articles.body:
13 de julho - Homem se exercita no Parque Ibirapuera, Zona Sul da cidade de São Paulo, nesta segunda-feira (13). O local foi reaberto depois de 111 dias fechado por causa da pandemia do coronavírus (Covid-19) — Foto: Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Um homem de 42 anos morreu após passar mal enquanto praticava atividade física, na manhã desta terça-feira (27), dentro do Parque Ibirapuera, Zona Sul de São Paulo .

Guardas municipais foram acionados para atender à ocorrência. De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, o homem teve um mal súbito e parou de respirar.

Uma equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros assumiu o atendimento, e o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado. O óbito foi constatado no local.

O caso foi registrado como morte suspeita no 27º Distrito Policial e está sendo apurado pelas equipes do delegado Ignácio Francisco.

Por meio de nota, a concessionária Urbia lamentou o "falecimento de um visitante, ocorrido por mal súbito na manhã desta terça-feira (27), no Parque Ibirapuera".

"O Corpo de Bombeiros e as equipes do Parque foram prontamente acionados e prestaram assistência imediata no local. Apesar dos esforços de atendimento, ele infelizmente não resistiu. A concessionária se solidariza com os familiares e amigos neste momento de pesar", disse a empresa.

articles.title: Filha de cantora pioneira da música gospel se declaraà mãe | G1
articles.standfirst: Harpista Aline Araújo publicou uma foto segurando a mão de Sara Araújo e afirmou que as duas nunca mais vão se separar. Cantora morreu aos 80 anos, em Goiânia.
articles.summary: Harpista Aline Araújo publicou uma foto segurando a mão de Sara Araújo e afirmou que as duas nunca mais vão se separar. Cantora morreu aos 80 anos, em Goiânia.
articles.body:
A harpista Aline Araújo publicou uma homenagem à mãe, a cantora gospel Sara Araújo, que morreu aos 80 anos, em Goiânia no sábado (24). Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, Aline compartilhou uma foto em que aparece segurando a mão da mãe e se declarou.

“Mamãe você é meu coração, minha alma gêmea. Vou para o céu mamãe e nunca mais vamos nos separar”.

Em outra postagem a família informou que Aline não está conseguindo falar com ninguém neste momento de dor. A publicação também anunciou que o perfil da harpista no Instagram será desativado na sexta-feira (30).

Sara adotou Aline em um orfanato. A cantora também foi a principal inspiração da filha na música e a apoiou durante a trajetória para se tornar harpista.

Aline ainda relatou as dificuldades enfrentadas pelas duas para conseguir uma harpa sinfônica. Segundo a filha, Sara produzia artesanatos para ajudar a custear as despesas e permitir que Aline representasse Goiás em um festival internacional de harpa.

De acordo com Aline, um dos sonhos de Sara era ver a filha realizar um concerto em Goiás.

Sara morreu no sábado (24). A artista foi velada e enterrada na tarde de domingo (25), no Cemitério Vale do Cerrado, em Goiânia. A causa da morte não foi informada pela família.

Filha de cantora gospel se declara para mãe — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Sara Araújo e Aline Araújo

Sara Araújo foi uma das pioneiras da música gospel no Brasil. Ao longo da carreira, gravou 40 discos. A cantora também atuou como missionária da Igreja Assembleia de Deus por 65 anos.

Além da música, Sara desenvolveu um trabalho social. Segundo Aline, a mãe fundou a Creche Comunitária Esperança, em Uberlândia, Minas Gerais, que atualmente presta assistência a 100 crianças.

A morte de Sara também motivou homenagens de artistas e pessoas ligadas à música gospel nas redes sociais.

A cantora Tangela Vieira publicou um vídeo em que aparece cantando ao lado de Sara. Em outra homenagem, uma publicação relembrou um momento em que a artista cantou um hino de Débora Miranda ao lado da própria cantora.

O Instituto Hinologia Cristã também lamentou a morte de Sara e destacou a importância dela para a história da música sacra no Brasil. Mensagens publicadas nas redes sociais destacaram a trajetória musical da cantora e manifestaram solidariedade.

articles.title: Lula cresce 3 vezes mais que Flávio Bolsonaro em Juiz de Fora | G1
articles.standfirst: Comparação dos resultados mostra que o petista foi o candidato que mais ganhou apoio entre os turnos e ampliou desempenho em diversas regiões de Juiz de Fora.
articles.summary: Lula Juiz de Fora eleições: petista cresceu 22% entre os turnos e conquistou 13 bairros onde Flávio Bolsonaro havia vencido anteriormente.
articles.body:
Lula discursa na avenida Paulista — Foto: REUTERS

Lula (PT) foi o candidato que mais avançou entre o primeiro e o segundo turno das Eleições 2026 em Juiz de Fora . Além de manter a liderança geral no município, o crescimento do petista foi mais de três vezes superior ao registrado pelo adversário na etapa final da disputa presidencial.

Com 151.552 votos na cidade no primeiro turno e 184.952 no segundo, Lula cresceu 22% entre os dois dias de votação. Já Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) passou de 126.964 para 135.835 entre os turnos, um aumento de 7% . Nessa perspectiva, o petista ampliou os votos em Juiz de Fora em 3,14 vezes mais que o bolsonarista .

A comparação dos resultados mostra que Lula conseguiu ampliar a votação em todos os bairros onde já era competitivo e ainda atraiu parte do eleitorado que havia optado por outros candidatos ou mesmo pelo voto branco e nulo e pela abstenção no primeiro turno. O movimento permitiu ao petista ampliar a diferença em diversos pontos da cidade e fortalecer ainda mais a presença eleitoral em Juiz de Fora .

Confira no gráfico abaixo o desempenho dos dois candidatos nos dois turnos em Juiz de Fora.

O segundo turno consolidou um cenário de aumento em todas as localidades da cidade, além de ter virado votos em 13 dos 16 bairros onde Flávio Bolsonaro havia liderado no primeiro turno .

Na prática, a velocidade de crescimento do petista significativamente maior entre uma etapa e outra da eleição, deixou o mapa de Juiz de Fora praticamente todo vermelho, com apenas três pequenos pontos azuis .

Confira abaixo, no mapa interativo, como o seu bairro votou no 1º e no 2º turno e compare o desempenho dos candidatos em cada região da cidade.

articles.title: Argentina diz que não tem registro da entrada de Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Polícia Federal apura se senador deixou o Brasil. No domingo (25), decisão do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do STF, proibiu-o de deixar o país. Um assessor do presidente argentino, Javier Milei, negou à Bloomberg que o senador brasileiro tenha entrado no país.
articles.summary: Decisão do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do STF, proíbe Flávio de deixar o Brasil.
articles.body:
O controle de imigrações do governo Milei afirmou nesta terça-feira (27) que não há registro de entrada do senador Flávio Bolsonaro na Argentina . A informação começou a circular após o site argentino Infobae publicar que Flávio teria entrado no país e que pegaria um voo particular de lá para os Estados Unidos.

"Informamos que não há registro de entrada de Flávio Nantes Bolsonaro no país", afirmou ao g1 a Direção Nacional de Imigrações do governo argentino.

Em nota, o órgão afirmou que iniciou procedimentos de fiscalização da aeronave citada pela reportagem e de sua tripulação, e que "não foi apresentado nenhum plano de voo que incluísse membros da família Bolsonaro".

A Direção Nacional de Migrações da Argentina (DNM) é o órgão federal responsável pelo controle migratório no país e é subordinado ao Ministério da Segurança Nacional argentino.

Segundo o blog da Andreia Sadi, a Polícia Federal brasileira está investigando se Flávio deixou o país rumo à Argentina. Até o momento, fontes da PF de Foz do Iguaçu afirmam que não havia registro da passagem de Flávio pela fronteira.

Um porta-voz de Javier Milei negou à agência de notícias norte-americana Bloomberg que Flávio Bolsonaro tenha entrado na Argentina.

Segundo a reportagem do Infobae, Bolsonaro teria cruzado a fronteira para a Argentina usando seu documento de identidade. "De Puerto Iguazú, viajaria aos Estados Unidos a bordo de um avião Gulfstream G400, de matrícula LV-JQW, pertencente à empresa Baires Fly S.A", informa o site.

Segundo o site de monitoramento aéreo FlightRadar24, a aeronave LV-JQW, citada pelo Infobae, voou de Buenos Aires para Puerto Iguazú e chegou à cidade às 23h45, no horário de Brasília.

O avião, no entanto, não havia deixado a cidade desde então, segundo os registros. O FlightRadar24, no entanto, dá opção para que voos privados optem por não aparecer na plataforma de rastreamento.

O g1 entrou em contato com o gabinete de Javier Milei, com o Ministério das Relações Exteriores argentino e com a Baires Fly, mas não recebeu resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Flávio Bolsonaro em pronunciamento após perder eleição. — Foto: Agustin Marcarian/Reuters

O ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou que Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) entregue seus passaportes. A decisão foi dada na noite do domingo (25) em processo em que Flávio Bolsonaro e o advogado Willer Tomaz são investigados por lavagem de dinheiro, em um suposto esquema que envolveria empresas de Tomaz e bets.

Os dois confirmam que são amigos, mas negam que sejam sócios - e qualquer irregularidade.

Flávio Bolsonaro também é formalmente investigado pela Polícia Federal (PF) em inquérito aberto para apurar a possível prática de crimes relacionados ao financiamento da produção do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a trajetória do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Quase 9 mil clientes ainda estão sem energia em BH após temporal | G1
articles.standfirst: Na Grande BH, o número de clientes sem energia chega a 16.797. Segundo a Cemig, 95% dos 640 mil consumidores afetados, em Minas Gerais, desde domingo (25) já tiveram o serviço restabelecido mas não informou prazo para normalização do serviço.
articles.summary: Na Grande BH, o número de clientes sem energia chega a 16.797. Cemig não informou prazo para normalização do serviço.
articles.body:
Quase 9 mil clientes ainda estavam sem energia elétrica em Belo Horizonte na manhã desta terça-feira (27), dois dias após o início das fortes tempestades que atingiram Minas Gerais. Segundo a Cemig, 8.765 consumidores permaneciam sem o serviço na capital, apesar de 98% do fornecimento afetado já ter sido restabelecido.

Silvana Lima, moradora do bairro Jardim Vitória, em Belo Horizonte, afirma que está sem energia elétrica desde domingo (25), após a queda de uma árvore durante o temporal ( veja a foto abaixo ).

"Situação difícil, falta energia aqui no nosso bairro desde domingo, por volta de meio-dia, após a queda de uma árvore que atingiu um transformador na Rua Marrocos Filho", disse Silvana.

Moradora mostra situação no Jardim Vitória após temporal em BH. — Foto: Redes sociais

Na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, o número de clientes ainda sem energia chegava a 16.797 nesta terça . De acordo com a companhia, 96% dos consumidores afetados na Grande BH já tiveram o serviço normalizado.

A Cemig não informou previsão para o restabelecimento total do fornecimento . A empresa afirma que algumas ocorrências exigem intervenções mais complexas, incluindo a reconstrução de estruturas da rede elétrica danificadas durante os temporais.

Em todo o estado, 32.121 clientes permaneciam sem energia na manhã desta terça. Desde domingo (25), cerca de 640 mil consumidores foram afetados, dos quais mais de 607 mil já tiveram o fornecimento restabelecido, segundo a Cemig.

Segundo o Centro de Meteorologia da própria Cemig, foram registradas mais de 60 mil descargas atmosféricas , volume seis vezes superior ao esperado para uma tempestade habitual.

Também foram registradas fortes rajadas de vento em diferentes pontos do estado. Em BH, os ventos chegaram a quase 90 km/h. Segundo a empresa, raios, ventos e quedas de árvores provocaram danos à rede elétrica e dificultaram os trabalhos de recuperação.

A Cemig informou ainda que mantém cerca de 4,6 mil profissionais mobilizados . As equipes trabalham na reconstrução de trechos da rede, substituição de equipamentos danificados e retirada de árvores e galhos sobre a fiação.

articles.title: Oiapoque enfrenta falta de energia após problema em usina na região  | G1
articles.standfirst: Energia foi interrompida durante a madrugada. Em nota, a Oiapoque Energia informou que o fornecimento foi restabelecido e que apura o ocorrido.
articles.summary: Energia foi interrompida durante a madrugada. Em nota, a Oiapoque Energia informou que o fornecimento foi restabelecido e que apura o ocorrido.
articles.body:
Município de Oiapoque, norte do Amapá — Foto: Fecomércio/Divulgação

O município de Oiapoque , no extremo norte do Amapá , enfrentou horas de apagão nesta terça-feira (27). A interrupção no fornecimento causou transtornos à população e afetou atividades comerciais e serviços na cidade.

Moradores relataram dificuldades de comunicação e informaram que só conseguiam acessar a internet ou realizar chamadas em estabelecimentos que possuíam geradores.

Em nota, a Oiapoque Energia informou que o fornecimento já foi restabelecido. A empresa afirmou que continua investigando as causas da ocorrência e reforçou o compromisso com a qualidade e a continuidade dos serviços prestados.

Logo que o problema foi identificado, a Cea Equatorial informou que a interrupção do fornecimento foi provocada por uma ocorrência na usina operada pela empresa responsável pela geração elétrica na região.

Segundo a distribuidora, equipes avaliaram os componentes da unidade para identificar a causa da falha. A concessionária afirmou ainda que acompanhava a situação e mantinha contato com a geradora.

Procurada pelo g1 , a Prefeitura de Oiapoque não se manifestou até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Seca em Oriximiná: cidade decreta emergência por estiagem extrema | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 37 mil pessoas são afetadas pela falta de água e isolamento no oeste do Pará. Comunidades já registram casos de diarreia e vômito por consumo de água inadequada.
articles.summary: Seca em Oriximiná isola comunidades e causa surtos de doenças, levando o município a decretar emergência para socorrer 37 mil pessoas no Pará.
articles.body:
Região do Lago Maria Pixi é uma das mais afetadas pela estiagem severa. — Foto: Divulgação: Silvio Printes

A Prefeitura de Oriximiná , no oeste do Pará, decretou situação de emergência por causa da seca histórica que atinge a região. A estiagem extrema isolou comunidades inteiras e já afeta cerca de 37.600 pessoas, incluindo indígenas, quilombolas, ribeirinhos e moradores da região do Planalto.

O decreto, assinado pelo prefeito Delegado Fonseca, tem validade inicial de 90 dias. Segundo a Defesa Civil do município, o nível dos rios baixou drasticamente, chegando a apenas 0,96 metro, marca que fica bem abaixo da cota de alerta de 1,50 metro. Com os rios secos, barcos não conseguem navegar, o que impede o transporte de alimentos e o deslocamento dos moradores.

A falta de água potável é um dos problemas mais graves enfrentados pela população. Em pelo menos 36 comunidades da região do Planalto, os moradores não têm água própria para o consumo. Devido ao uso de água inadequada, as autoridades de saúde já registraram surtos de diarreia e vômito em algumas localidades.

Para tentar conter a crise, o município planeja distribuir água potável, cestas básicas e kits de higiene para as famílias atingidas. O plano de resposta também prevê a compra de bombas elétricas e tubos para aprofundar poços artesianos e melhorar a captação de água nas áreas mais críticas.

Com o decreto de emergência, a prefeitura pode solicitar apoio técnico e financeiro aos governos estadual e federal de forma mais rápida. A medida também autoriza a contratação de serviços e a compra de materiais sem a necessidade de licitação, com o objetivo de agilizar o socorro às comunidades isoladas.

articles.title: Outubro Rosa: o cuidado que não pode ficar para depois | G1
articles.standfirst: Por Aguiar Farina, médico mastologista e presidente do Conselho de Administração da Unimed Cuiabá
articles.summary: Por Aguiar Farina, médico mastologista e presidente do Conselho de Administração da Unimed Cuiabá
articles.body:
Aguiar Farina, médico mastologista e presidente do Conselho de Administração da Unimed Cuiabá — Foto: Assessoria | Unimed Cuiabá

Existe uma característica do câncer de mama que merece nossa atenção: ele quase sempre não dói, nem sempre apresenta sinais perceptíveis e nem sempre interfere na rotina de quem está desenvolvendo a doença. É justamente essa ausência de sintomas, em muitos casos, que torna a prevenção e o diagnóstico precoce tão importantes. Esperar o corpo avisar pode significar perder um tempo precioso.

Como médico mastologista, aprendi que cuidar da saúde exige mais do que tratar uma doença quando ela aparece. Exige informação, acompanhamento e, sobretudo, a decisão de não adiar aquilo que pode fazer diferença no futuro. No Outubro Rosa, esse é o convite que precisamos reforçar: não espere sentir alguma coisa para olhar com atenção para a sua saúde.

O câncer de mama é uma das doenças que mais afetam as mulheres no Brasil. Embora não seja possível impedir todos os casos, identificar a doença precocemente aumenta as possibilidades de tratamento e pode melhorar significativamente os resultados. Por isso, consultas regulares e exames de rastreamento, indicados conforme a idade, o histórico familiar e os fatores de risco de cada mulher, são ferramentas fundamentais.

Mas existe um aspecto dessa discussão que merece ser observado: quantas vezes conseguimos organizar a rotina inteira, mas deixamos a própria saúde para quando sobrar tempo?

Trabalho, família, compromissos e responsabilidades ocupam nossos dias. Muitas mulheres cuidam dos filhos, acompanham os pais, sustentam suas casas e estão presentes para tantas pessoas que acabam colocando as próprias necessidades em último lugar. A consulta que seria marcada na segunda-feira fica para a próxima semana. O exame que deveria ser feito naquele mês passa para o seguinte. E, sem perceber, o adiamento se transforma em hábito.

O Outubro Rosa serve exatamente para isso, chamar a atenção para o cuidado preventivo, principalmente quando não há sintomas. Prevenção não é apenas uma campanha, uma cor ou uma mensagem compartilhada nas redes sociais. É uma atitude concreta, que começa quando cada mulher entende que cuidar de si não é egoísmo, mas uma necessidade.

Outro ponto importante é não confundir prevenção com a realização de um único exame. O cuidado envolve conhecer o próprio corpo, procurar avaliação médica diante de alterações nas mamas e manter o acompanhamento recomendado por profissionais de saúde. Mudanças como nódulos, retrações na pele, alterações no mamilo ou saída espontânea de secreção merecem investigação. Ao mesmo tempo, é importante lembrar que muitas alterações podem ter causas benignas e que somente a avaliação médica permite esclarecer cada situação.

A mamografia tem papel essencial no rastreamento do câncer de mama, mas sua indicação deve considerar as recomendações vigentes e as características individuais. Mulheres com histórico familiar relevante ou outros fatores de risco podem precisar de acompanhamento diferenciado. Por isso, a orientação médica é indispensável para definir o momento adequado dos exames.

Também precisamos falar sobre acesso. Não basta dizer às mulheres que elas devem se cuidar se não houver condições para realizar consultas, exames e tratamentos em tempo oportuno. A prevenção precisa ser acompanhada de informação de qualidade, serviços acessíveis e uma rede de assistência preparada para acolher e orientar. É uma responsabilidade compartilhada entre profissionais de saúde, instituições, empresas, famílias e poder público.

Na Unimed Cuiabá, entendemos que promover saúde significa ir além do atendimento à doença. Significa valorizar a orientação, o acompanhamento e a conscientização, estimulando escolhas que contribuam para uma vida com mais qualidade. Esse compromisso precisa estar presente durante todo o ano, e não apenas em outubro.

Como médico, sei que cada diagnóstico tem uma história e que nenhuma experiência é igual à outra. Como presidente do Conselho de Administração, reconheço também a importância de fortalecer uma cultura de cuidado que coloque as pessoas no centro das decisões. Essas duas perspectivas se encontram em uma mesma convicção: informação e assistência no momento certo podem fazer a diferença.

Neste Outubro Rosa, proponho uma mudança simples de perspectiva. Em vez de perguntar apenas quando foi a última vez que você fez um exame, pergunte também por que continua adiando o próximo. Converse com seu médico, esclareça suas dúvidas e organize seu acompanhamento.

A saúde não deveria depender de uma brecha na agenda. Ela precisa fazer parte das nossas prioridades.

Porque o melhor momento para cuidar de si não é quando aparece um sinal de alerta. É enquanto você pode agir antes dele.

articles.title: Thorpe St Andrew School attacker 'radicalised online', says dad
articles.summary: A father calls for tighter controls on extreme material after his son's attempted murder conviction.
articles.body:
Warning: The following report contains details that some may find distressing

The father of a teenager who tried to kill a fellow pupil in a school knife attack has described his devastation and belief that his son was "radicalised" by extreme material online.

The boy, now 16, was found guilty of attempted murder last week after a trial heard how he harboured a hatred of women, had a fascination with serial killers and had planned to target others in the attack at Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich.

Speaking exclusively to the BBC and calling for tighter controls, the boy's father said he did not want to "absolve" his son but suggested online material and "a culture of violence and horror" had influenced him.

The government said it was committed to ensuring all children were safe from radicalisation and threats online, pointing to its Prevent anti-terrorism scheme and the Online Safety Act , which compels social media platforms to remove and prevent the spread of illegal content.

The boy cannot be identified due to his age, and nor can witnesses and the victim in the case.

His father, who we are calling John, apologised to the 15-year-old girl injured in the attack on 11 March, saying: "We're so very sorry for what happened."

John spoke of his fears that young men were being radicalised towards violence and hatred.

"You can think... it can never happen to my family or my son couldn't be involved, but that's what we thought and that wasn't the case," he said.

A two-week trial at King's Lynn Crown Court heard how the boy dressed in black and wore a face mask to stab the girl with a kitchen knife.

John described his own "rising feeling of panic" on the day of the attack.

He said he and his wife had been "fearful for what he might have done and fearful for what would happen to him".

But John said he only learned the full details when they emerged during the trial.

"It was awful, really devastating," he said.

He acknowledged the attack would have had "major repercussions" for the victim, who spent a night in hospital but was not seriously injured.

"I hope the victim and her family can sort of get over it as soon as possible in terms of healing and move on," he said.

Before the attack, John said, his family had been "normal".

His son was shy but had a group of friends and had been "kind and thoughtful" at home.

As a teenager, he began to spend more time on his own, but John saw nothing concerning.

However, police later found the boy had searched the internet for material on mass shootings and serial killers, including on the night before the attack - something John said he had "no idea" about.

"It was shocking and devastating that he would have been looking at that kind of stuff," he said.

While there were parental controls on his son's devices, these were mainly to limit screen time.

"There was nothing to indicate that anything sinister was going on," said John.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, you can visit the BBC Action Line for information and support

Asked if they should have known more about what was on their son's phone, he said: "I can see the argument.

"I doubt many parents will go through their kids' browsing history on a regular basis.

"Hindsight's a marvellous thing, isn't it?"

When police searched the family home after the attack, they found the boy had written notes planning a wider attack.

They talked about deaths and injuries, listing misanthropy, misogyny, suicide, bullying as motives.

John said reading the notes made him feel "physically sick".

"It's still perplexing to us that he would write those things and feel those things that he was feeling," he said.

"He just seems like a different person doing that; some different version of him that's emerged from whatever he's been watching or seeing online."

John said his son had told him he believed his interest in extreme violence began after he saw a clip on TikTok from TV drama Dexter, which tells the story of a vigilante serial killer.

"Once you watch one thing like that, the algorithm, of course, feeds you more of the same content," he said.

He said he believed some young men could be drawn towards increasingly extreme material online and called for tighter regulations on children's access to it.

"There's the radicalisation of young men in particular. They talk about it with regards to terrorism and political ideology, but [there's] a radicalisation towards violence and hatred," he said.

"There must be ways to block content or to monitor content. We see millions of pounds spent on other things. Is there enough being spent on this kind of thing?"

Ofcom, the official regulator for broadcasting and the internet, says it is the responsibility of tech firms to keep children safe online.

It says it is holding those companies to account, but has the following tips for parents :

Talk regularly to your children about what they do when they're online.

Make sure your children register with online services using their real age, to help prevent them from accessing content that is only suitable for people who are older.

Make sure they know how to report inappropriate or harmful content, how to block accounts that share it and encourage them not to share it themselves. If content is illegal, report it to the police.

Parental controls are a useful tool, helping you to monitor and limit the time your children spend online, and what they do when they're there.

The attack by John's son had parallels with the storyline of hit Netflix drama Adolescence, which shows the aftermath of the fatal stabbing of a teenage girl by a fellow school pupil.

It highlighted the corrosive impact of social media and misogynist influencers on some teenage boys and prompted then Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer to pledge to tackle the issue .

John said while he had not personally watched the show, he was aware of discussion around it and could see why links to it might be made.

"Knowing what it was about did prompt a chat with our son about the manosphere and those sort of toxic influencers it references," he said.

Notes written by John's son expressed a hatred of women, and he had also researched Elliot Rodger , described to jurors as "an early influence on incel and manosphere culture".

But John said his son had never shown evidence of misogyny.

"He's always got on well with all the women he's known in his life... there's never been a problem."

John said the family believed their son was dealing with mental health issues in the months before the attack.

He had wanted to self-harm and had attempted to take his own life, he said.

"We were worried about what he might do to himself."

John urged other parents not to be afraid to be "a bit intrusive" into their children's lives, adding: "Try and have a proper chat. It's difficult to find the time sometimes because you're wrapped up in your own things."

In a statement, a government spokesman said its thoughts were with the victim and all of those affected by the "terrible events" at Thorpe St Andrew School.

"We are committed to ensuring all children are safe from radicalisation and threats online," they said.

" Prevent plays a crucial role in this, moving more than 6,000 people away from violent ideologies since 2015.

"In addition, social media platforms must be able to remove illegal content and stop children accessing harmful material by law – or face penalties of up to £18m for failing to comply."

John acknowledged that his son was "looking at a long sentence" when he appears before the court again in December.

"We will support him as best we can, try and see that he gets the mental health support he needs and try and get back how he used to be," he said.

articles.title: Anti-social behaviour by neighbours has been 'hell', tenant says
articles.summary: Man calls for better support after seven years of anti-social behaviour from neighbours.
articles.body:
For seven years James Daniel has been living next to successive "nightmare neighbours". Despite numerous complaints to various agencies, including his housing association, he said his situation had not improved.

It comes as new data from the Housing Ombudsman showed a rise over five years in the number of complaints upheld about social landlords' handling of anti-social behaviour.

While Devon and Cornwall Police has increased the number of closure orders placed on residential properties, housing associations report that dealing with anti-social behaviour can be a complex issue and requires working closely with other agencies.

Daniel said he had spent years reporting the alleged anti-social behaviour and collecting evidence, including security camera and mobile phone footage, which he passed on to the police, North Devon Homes and now the BBC.

The videos he shared with the BBC showed knives being thrown from a window, an altercation outside his house and a neighbour appearing to make gun gestures at his security camera.

Other footage showed a previous tenant shouting at Daniel and other residents, as well as throwing bags of rubbish and a dust pan brush.

"Living next door to anti-social behaviour has been hell to be honest, absolute hell, said Daniel.

While Daniel said he had previously been offered a different property, he was reluctant to move.

"I don't feel it's something that anybody should have to do, is move from their home because of somebody else," he said.

The current neighbour is the second neighbour he has alleged has subjected him and his partner to significant anti-social behaviour.

North Devon Homes said all reports of anti-social behaviour were taken seriously and that it recognised the "significant impact" it could have on those affected.

It said it was working closely with customers and partner agencies to "investigate concerns, provide support and take appropriate action" where necessary.

New data showed the Housing Ombudsman upheld almost four times as many complaints relating to social landlords' handling of anti-social behaviour reports than five years ago.

In the 2021-2022 financial year, the ombudsman found failings in 159 incidents compared with 609 in 2025–26.

Ric Blakeway, the Housing Ombudsman at the time, said there were a number of "consistent reasons" why the maladministration rate - or uphold rate - had increased.

"It's poor communication, it's poor record keeping, it's not using the tools that landlords should use - such as doing a risk assessment or producing an action plan - and that is a consistent reason that we would uphold a case," he explained.

"Where we don't uphold it though, I think you see the kind of opposite of that."

Easier access to the ombudsman service and greater awareness of housing rights were among the drivers Blakeway believed had led to a rise in casework.

Blakeway said his teams had seen cases where residents had been making themselves "in effect homeless" by sleeping in cars to escape the anti-social behaviour.

Where the ombudsman finds failure, it can force housing associations or councils to take action, write apologies or pay compensation to the tenant.

Daniel has taken his case to the ombudsman and is awaiting a determination.

A spokesperson for North Devon Homes said it had fully cooperated with the investigation and looked forward to the Ombudsman's findings.

One tactic being increasingly used by Devon and Cornwall Police to tackle anti-social behaviour is closure orders.

This is where the force can apply to a court for the power to remove a resident from the address for at least three months in what it calls a "full closure".

In most cases, the force says the owner of the property then has the chance to regain control of the property, or the tenant can move back in.

A "partial closure" means the resident can stay at the address but no visitors are allowed in.

Machaela O'Brien, legal advisor for Devon and Cornwall Police, said closure orders could provide an "immediate remedy" but were a "draconian measure".

"What we find is that closure orders are a really good temporary solution to address any problem premises," O'Brien explained.

She added support was provided to people removed from a property and they were "signposted to relevant agencies", including the council and social services.

Evicting a tenant through the court system can be a time consuming and costly process for landlords.

In West Cornwall, neighbours said closure orders on two properties in the same street had been effective.

Melanie, whose surname we are not using, said residents had been "living in fear" before one neighbour, who was accused of waving a sword, was removed.

"You shouldn't have to live like that these days," she said.

At another property, PC James Tompson said officers spent weeks gathering evidence of drug use, fighting and anti-social behaviour linked to the address.

In April, Daniel's neighbour was convicted of assaulting another resident and a month later was charged with allegedly harassing him.

Daniel said victims of anti-social behaviour, particularly in social housing, needed support from agencies in a "more joined up approach".

"For me, it's about highlighting the system is broken," he said.

"All the agencies are involved but actually it seems nobody's talking to each other, and nobody knows what's going on."

He said he no longer felt safe at home and that it was becoming "impossible to get any support" for those affected by anti-social behaviour.

"It's got to the point where actually the house that I love, I don't love anymore," he added.

The National Housing Federation said anti-social behaviour cases could be "serious and complex" and housing associations took them very seriously.

Blakeway said it was "really, really important that we see an improvement to the way in which different bodies are working together to try and resolve cases".

North Devon Homes, Daniel's housing provider, said: "Cases involving individuals with severe and complex vulnerabilities can be particularly challenging, requiring organisations to work within legal frameworks and statutory processes while balancing the needs and safety of all those involved."

Additional reporting by Ema Sabljak, BBC England Data Unit.

articles.title: Israel heads into deeply divided election as Oct 7 reckoning looms: What to know
articles.summary: Will Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hold power? Israel's election becomes a referendum on Oct. 7 failures as no bloc secures a clear majority.
articles.body: TEL AVIV, ISRAEL — Campaign banners bearing the faces of Israel's political leaders cover buildings and roadsides, while in homes, coffee shops and family gatherings, the same question dominates conversations: Will Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remain in power? With Israelis heading to the polls Tuesday, the country is bracing for a closely contested election that could end in another political deadlock. But this vote is unlike any other in Israel's recent history. For many Israelis, the election has become a referendum on accountability for the failures that allowed Hamas terrorists to carry out the Oct. 7, 2023, massacre — the deadliest attack in Israel's history. TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE Netanyahu, who has dominated Israeli politics for decades, has resisted calls to accept personal responsibility for the security failures and establish an independent state commission of inquiry. His government instead sought a politically appointed investigation, a proposal fiercely opposed by many bereaved families. Yet Israel's divisions began long before Oct. 7. In the months preceding the attacks, hundreds of thousands of Israelis took to the streets to protest Netanyahu's proposed judicial overhaul, which critics argued would undermine the country's democracy. The confrontation spilled into the military, where reservists threatened to suspend volunteer service, raising alarms about Israel's preparedness. Some critics have argued that the turmoil projected weakness to the country's enemies, although the extent to which it influenced Hamas's decision to attack remains disputed. Three years after the massacre, those divisions have only deepened, transforming Tuesday's vote into something intensely personal. Political allegiances have strained friendships and divided families, with much of the national debate reduced to a single question: Are you for Netanyahu, widely known as "Bibi," or against him? DANNY DANON: FROM OCT 7 TO FLIGHT 1073: THE RESILIENCE THAT KEEPS ISRAEL STANDING For some families who lost loved ones on Oct. 7, the answer is painfully clear. Shir Shai, whose brother Yaron Shai, an Israeli soldier, was killed battling Hamas terrorists that day, delivered a stark message to those considering another vote for Netanyahu. "If you nevertheless decide to vote again for the man who brought disaster upon us and his accomplices, I have one personal request: Don't come here anymore," Shai said over her brother's grave in his memorial ceremony on October 7. "You still have 20 days to be part of the process of putting things right. But if you choose to perpetuate the failure rather than honor the fallen, it would be better if you stayed home next year," she added. NETANYAHU PRAISES TRUMP'S 'WICKED SENSE OF HUMOR,' DEFENDS IRONCLAD ALLIANCE AHEAD OF HISTORIC ISRAEL VOTE Yet other bereaved families have reached the opposite conclusion, crediting Netanyahu with standing firm through years of war on multiple fronts and arguing that Israel's military and intelligence establishment bears the principal responsibility for failing to anticipate the Hamas assault. The deeply polarized atmosphere has been intensified by an increasingly bitter campaign. Just two days before the election, Netanyahu shared an AI-generated image depicting a nuclear explosion over Tel Aviv, warning of the existential threat posed by Iran if the country elects a leader unable to confront Tehran. Concerns now extend beyond the election results themselves. Israeli police are preparing for possible unrest after the polls close, while experts have warned about the potential for disputes over the legitimacy of the results — including an extreme scenario resembling the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol. With the opposition united in its ambition to replace Netanyahu but divided over how to govern afterward, neither political bloc is assured of a parliamentary majority and the final outcome could take weeks to determine. JD VANCE DECLINES TO ENDORSE NETANYAHU DESPITE TRUMP'S STRONG BACKING When do polls open and close? Israelis will vote Tuesday, Oct. 27, with most polling stations opening at 7 a.m. and closing at 10 p.m. local time. Election Day is a national holiday in Israel, giving voters the opportunity to cast their ballots. Some smaller communities and special polling locations operate on different schedules. Eligible voters must be Israeli citizens at least 18 years old and generally vote at their assigned polling station. Most Israelis living abroad cannot vote remotely, although exceptions apply to certain official representatives overseas. How does Israel's election system work? Israel has a parliamentary system in which voters select a political party rather than an individual candidate for prime minister. The country's parliament, known as the Knesset, has 120 seats, distributed through a system of nationwide proportional representation. Each party submits a ranked list of candidates, and the number of seats it receives depends on its share of the national vote. To enter parliament, a party must win at least 3.25% of the valid votes. Parties falling below that threshold receive no seats, potentially changing the balance between rival political blocs. IRAN IS TRYING TO ‘CREATE A ROT FROM WITHIN’ THROUGH ‘INFORMATION WARFARE,’ ANALYST WARNS When will election results be announced? Israel's major television networks are expected to release exit polls immediately after voting ends at 10 p.m. Tuesday (4 p.m. EST). Those projections will provide the first indication of how many seats each party may win and whether Netanyahu or his rivals appear better positioned to assemble a coalition. But exit polls are not official results, and even small differences in the final vote could determine whether parties cross the electoral threshold. Actual vote counts will emerge as ballots are counted, with preliminary results developing after polls close and over the following days. Israel's Central Elections Committee has scheduled the publication of official results for Wednesday, Nov. 4, eight days after the election. Who are the main candidates? Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, 77, leads the conservative right-wing Likud party and is seeking to extend his record tenure as Israel's longest-serving prime minister. His main challenger is Gadi Eisenkot, 66, a former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces who leads the centrist Yashar party and has positioned himself as an alternative to Netanyahu's leadership. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, 54, is also seeking a political comeback, running on a joint ticket with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid. Other significant political figures include former Defense Minister Avigdor Lieberman, Democrats leader Yair Golan and Netanyahu's right-wing populist allies Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. Arab political parties, including Ra'am and the Joint List, could also play a crucial role in determining the final parliamentary balance. How many seats does a party need to win? The key number in Israeli politics is 61 — a majority of the 120-seat Knesset. No single Israeli party has ever won enough seats to control parliament alone, meaning parties generally need to form coalitions with other political factions. This means the party that wins the most seats does not automatically get to lead the government. Instead, the decisive question is which political leader can secure enough parliamentary support to govern. How is Israel's next prime minister chosen? Once the official results are published, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will consult representatives of the newly elected parliamentary factions. Within seven days, the president must assign a member of the Knesset the task of forming a government. The president generally selects the politician considered most likely to assemble a governing coalition, who is not necessarily the leader of the largest party. That candidate initially has 28 days to reach agreements with other parties, with the possibility of an extension of up to 14 additional days. The proposed government must then win a confidence vote in the Knesset before taking office. What happens if nobody can form a government? If the first candidate fails, the president can ask another lawmaker to attempt to form a government, giving that person 28 days without an extension. If that effort also fails, a majority of 61 lawmakers can request that another candidate be given 14 days to try. If no government emerges, Israel could face another national election. Coalition negotiations can take weeks or months. According to the Israel Democracy Institute, the process of forming an Israeli government has historically taken between 20 and 100 days. Until a new government is sworn in, the outgoing government remains in office. Why is this election particularly consequential? Tuesday's vote is the first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, which triggered the war in Gaza and raised profound questions about Israel's security leadership. Beyond Netanyahu's political future, the next government will face decisions over Israel's national security, the future of Gaza, military conscription, relations with the United States and the country's regional diplomatic relationships. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP With pre-election polling showing no clear path to a parliamentary majority for either major political bloc, the contest could remain unresolved long after Tuesday's votes are counted.

articles.title: India evacuates tens of thousands as ‘very severe’ Cyclone Arnab nears
articles.summary: The cyclonic storm is set to make landfall on Wednesday, with 400,000 people in need of evacuation.
articles.body:
India is evacuating tens of thousands of people from its eastern coast as a strengthening Cyclone Arnab bears down on its coastal states.

The cyclone has intensified since Monday and is expected to make landfall by Wednesday morning.

The India Meteorological Department has issued a warning for the coastal states of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, saying the “very severe” cyclonic storm was centred only 260km (160 miles) southeast of the port city of Visakhapatnam, the most populous in Andhra Pradesh.

The department expects Arnab to turn northwest and cross the coast by 11:30am local time (06:00 GMT) on Wednesday, with sustained winds of 115-125km/h (71-78mph) and gusts of up to 140km/h (87mph).

Arnab formed over the Bay of Bengal, which is among the world’s main breeding grounds for tropical cyclones, frequently affecting India’s eastern coastal regions.

More than 12 million people live along the cyclone’s projected path, which runs inland and north across India, according to Andhra Pradesh’s disaster management authority.

Nearly 50,000 people had been moved to shelters from vulnerable areas of the state by Monday night, out of an estimated 400,000 in need of evacuation, the authority’s managing director, Prakhar Jain, told the Reuters news agency.

Railway authorities in the region said on social media that at least 12 trains had been cancelled in eastern India and services on 53 routes along the southern coast had been suspended for Tuesday and Wednesday.

In Odisha, authorities have announced plans to evacuate 48,000 people out of harm’s way, according to local newspaper The Hindu.

Authorities in neighbouring Nepal have advised tourists to stay away from high-altitude areas over concerns that Arnab could trigger heavy rain, snowstorms and avalanches in the Himalayas from Thursday night to Saturday.

The advisory comes after a Himalayan flash flood in August killed about 1,500 people in the country.

articles.title: In 1985, Dionne Warwick, Elton John, Gladys Knight and Stevie Wonder recorded a charity hit; the song helped raise millions for AIDS research as the epidemic was unfolding
articles.summary: In 1985, as the AIDS epidemic spread and fear and misinformation surrounded the disease, four of the biggest names in music came together to record a song
articles.body: In 1985, as the AIDS epidemic spread and fear and misinformation surrounded the disease, four of the biggest names in music came together to record a song that would become a landmark charity hit. Dionne Warwick, Elton John, Gladys Knight and Stevie Wonder joined forces on That's What Friends Are For, turning a song about friendship and support into a fundraising effort for AIDS research. Released under the name Dionne & Friends, the single became a major commercial success, eventually raising millions of dollars for the American Foundation for AIDS Research, known as amfAR. It also earned major Grammy recognition, giving the campaign a reach far beyond the recording studio.How four music legends came togetherThe song was written by Burt Bacharach and Carole Bayer Sager and had originally been recorded by Rod Stewart for the 1982 film Night Shift. When Warwick took up the song for the charity project, the idea developed into a collaboration featuring Elton John, Gladys Knight and Stevie Wonder.The performers brought together distinct musical styles, creating a recording whose message of loyalty and solidarity resonated with listeners. The project was supported by Bacharach, Bayer Sager and record executive Clive Davis, with proceeds directed towards AIDS research. The single was released in 1985, at a time when public understanding of HIV/AIDS remained limited and the need for research funding was urgent.Why the song mattered during the AIDS epidemicIn the early 1980s, AIDS had become a growing public-health crisis, but the disease was still widely misunderstood. The first recognised cases in the US were reported in 1981. Researchers were working to understand the virus, develop diagnostic tools and identify effective treatments, while people affected by the epidemic often faced discrimination and social isolation.A significant scientific milestone came in March 1985, when the US Food and Drug Administration approved the first commercial blood test to detect HIV. The test helped identify infections and made it possible to screen donated blood more effectively. However, effective long-term treatment remained unavailable, and the epidemic continued to claim lives.Against this backdrop, a charity recording featuring four internationally recognised performers helped bring AIDS research to a much wider audience. Its impact extended beyond its message: the commercial success of the single generated substantial funds for research and helped keep the cause in the public eye.How much money did the charity hit raise?The recording raised approximately $3.4 million for AIDS research, according to the Recording Academy's retrospective on Bacharach's career. Other accounts describe the total more generally as more than $3 million. The money supported amfAR, an organisation established in 1985 that became a prominent funder of AIDS research and an advocate for people affected by HIV/AIDS.The fundraising achievement was especially significant because the song reached audiences who might not otherwise have engaged directly with the issue. Its success demonstrated how the music industry could use a commercially popular release to generate money and attention for a public-health cause.The song's success continued at the GrammysThat's What Friends Are For became a major hit in the US, reaching No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1986. It went on to win two awards at the 1987 Grammy Awards: Song of the Year, awarded to songwriters Bacharach and Bayer Sager, and Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal, awarded to Warwick, John, Knight and Wonder.The awards cemented the recording's place in popular music history. But its legacy was not limited to chart positions or industry recognition. The song became closely associated with a moment when artists used their collective influence to support AIDS research at a time of immense uncertainty.A musical legacy beyond the chartsThe significance of That's What Friends Are For lies in the combination of its message, its star-studded collaboration and its fundraising impact. The recording did not solve the AIDS crisis or directly produce a medical breakthrough, but it helped finance research and raise awareness when both were urgently needed.Decades later, the song remains a prominent example of how popular music can support a charitable cause. Its message of friendship took on a broader meaning during the epidemic, offering a reminder of the importance of solidarity with people affected by a disease that was still poorly understood.You use AI every day. articles.title: Drone strike in Sudan’s Nyala kills at least 21, injures 40
articles.summary: Drone hit a market in the city that serves as the de facto capital of the paramilitary RSF in Darfur, resident says.
articles.body:
A drone strike in Nyala, in Sudan’s Darfur region, has killed at least 21 people and injured 40 others, the AFP news agency reported, citing a medical source and witnesses.

A Nyala resident said the attack took place at about 8pm (18:00 GMT) on Monday at a market in the north of the city, which serves as the de facto capital of Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

“Twenty-one people were killed in last night’s bombing, and more than 40 others injured,” a medic at Nyala Hospital said on Tuesday.

Another Nyala resident told AFP that the market was frequented by armed men, particularly RSF fighters.

The Sudanese military, which has been at war with the RSF since April 2023, regularly strikes Nyala, where the RSF has declared an administration rivalling the military-backed, internationally recognised government in Khartoum.

The attack comes as the warring sides are increasingly turning to drone warfare .

Earlier this month, the RSF launched strikes targeting Khartoum’s airport, as well as dams and power stations in the government-controlled east.

An RSF drone attack on Tuesday “targeted the al-Markhiyat transformer station, disrupting power supplies for millions across large parts of Khartoum and Gezira state”, a national electricity company told AFP on condition of anonymity.

It followed Monday’s coordinated RSF drone strikes on six power stations, which cut off electricity to millions in the states of Gezira, White Nile, Sennar and Gadarif.

A government drone attack in a disputed border region between Sudan and South Sudan earlier this month killed more than 150 people .

The war began in 2023 when a dispute over how to integrate the two forces erupted into clashes in the capital, Khartoum. The fighting has killed tens of thousands of people, displaced more than 13 million, and created the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

On Monday, the United States, the European Union and 30 other countries warned of an “ alarming deterioration ” in food access in Sudan and called for “urgent action” to prevent famine.

In a joint statement released by the US State Department on Monday, the signatories called on the groups fighting Sudan’s civil war “to lift all impediments on humanitarian assistance”.

articles.title: Two charged over alleged plot to assist Iran in RAF Fairford incident
articles.summary: Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, both 24, will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Two British nationals have been charged over an alleged plot to assist Iran's intelligence service as part of the investigation into the incident at RAF Fairford in September.

Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, 24, from Westminster, has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service under Section 3 of the National Security Act.

Nouman Essghir, also 24 and from Westminster, has been charged under Section 4 of the same act with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on 22 August - weeks before he was arrested near the airbase in Gloucestershire alongside four other men.

The pair will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near the US-operated airbase on 27 September.

Dozens of residents were evacuated and a large cordon was put up in the area around the base. No explosive materials were found in the vans by police but a quantity of petrol was seized.

Essghir, from Westminster, was one of five men arrested near the scene in Gloucestershire on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act and later on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act. All five were released on police bail the following day, but Essghir was re-arrested on 20 October.

A 25-year-old UK-Iranian national who was also re-arrested on that date on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service has now been released without charge. He remains on police bail after his initial arrest on 1 October on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts.

The re-arrests in October led to detectives interviewing Abdulkarim.

Eight men have been arrested as part of the counter-terror police investigation.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the release of the five men on police bail in September had raised significant questions and speculation about the investigation for members of the public.

He stressed that tactics used by counter-terror police can appear "illogical" at times but said that "there will always be a good reason or rationale behind them".

"In this case, this decision-making has led to swifter progress, better evidence, and ultimately us securing the charges that I've announced today," he added.

US President Donald Trump at the time said he was "surprised" the men had been released, saying: "We would not have released them."

Taylor said counter-terror police had seen "a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state".

Iran has previously denied any involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford.

The base has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base to the Middle East, after the UK approved a request for it to be used for defensive strikes against Iran.

After the incident in September the US pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America.

Trump said the aircraft were removed due to "some threats" to the base, without giving specific details.

articles.title: UK prosecutors charge two after RAF Fairford incident
articles.summary: British Iranian Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir have been charged under the National Security Act.
articles.body:
British prosecutors say they ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠have charged two men with ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌offences under the National Security Act following an incident ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠in September ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠at RAF Fairford, an ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠airbase in England used ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠by ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠the United States.

British Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir, both aged 24, were charged under the National Security Act, the Crown Prosecution Service said. They are due to appear in court later on Tuesday.

Abdulkarim is charged with engaging in conduct that was likely ‌to materially assist a foreign intelligence service. Assistant Commissioner Laurence ‌‌‌‌Taylor, head of the United Kingdom’s Counter Terrorism Policing, said police believed ‌‌‌‌the country ‌‌‌‌Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran.

Essghir was charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK.

Both men live in Westminster, a district in London.

The airbase in Gloucestershire, southwestern England, had been used by US bombers to carry out attacks on Iran this year.

Essghir was arrested outside the base on September 27, when armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Dozens of residents were evacuated from their homes as police and experts searched for explosives.

Abdulkarim was arrested in the past week. Six other men remain on bail, all living in London and aged between 23 and 25, as investigations continue.

Shortly after the incident at the base, US B-1 bombers were withdrawn from the site.

“We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state and, as the Director General of MI5 said just ‌the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” Taylor said in a ⁠statement.

Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec, reporting from London, said police initially commented that they were considering all avenues and that they were not ruling out a state actor.

“But at the time, they didn’t go so far as to point towards Iran – although US President Donald Trump and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham were fairly quick to say they believed that there was credible evidence to suggest Iran was involved,” she said.

“It’s only in the past few days that police who have been in charge of this investigation have increasingly said they believe there is evidence that Iran is involved,” she added.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham last week said the activity at RAF Fairford was likely to have been coordinated in Iran, which Iran’s ambassador to the UK has denied.

Last year, the UK said there had been 20 credible Iranian-backed threats to kill or kidnap individuals based in the UK.

In July, Britain used new powers to ban support for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and a linked group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI), which had claimed responsibility for seven attacks earlier this year at locations linked to Jewish and Israeli communities and Persian-language media.

articles.title: Israel election results 2026: When will we know who won and what’s next?
articles.summary: Exit polls are expected soon after voting closes late on Tuesday, but a final verdict might take days.
articles.body:
Israelis are voting in a closely watched election to decide on the direction of the country, three years after the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack on southern Israel that set off the genocidal war on Gaza.

The first election since those attacks comes at a time when Israel’s pogroms in the occupied West Bank have escalated, and amid mounting tensions with several of its neighbours, many of whom it has attacked in the past three years.

But the vote also comes amid growing domestic questions that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces over alleged failures that allowed the October 7 attack, his government’s handling of efforts to retrieve captives taken to Gaza, alleged corruption and disputes over ultra-Orthodox military service .

In final polls published Friday, Netanyahu’s coalition is expected to be neck and neck with – or trail slightly behind – the opposition bloc led by former Israeli military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot.

According to Israeli news outlet Haaretz, which has collated polls from Israeli news channels, as of Friday, an average of Channels 11, 12 and 13 predicts Netanyahu’s bloc will win 50 seats while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc will take 54 seats. The Israeli parliament, known as the Knesset, has 120 seats in all, so 61 is the mark that a grouping needs to reach a majority.

Here’s what you need to know about the election.

On Tuesday, polls opened at 7am local time (05:00 GMT) and will end at 10pm (20:00 GMT).

About 7.3 million Israelis will be eligible to vote, including 1.2 million Palestinian citizens of Israel. Israelis living abroad cannot vote because the country does not have a general absentee ballot, requiring voters to be physically present on election day.

Diplomats and state emissaries are the exception and cast their ballots at Israeli missions on October 20.

When will Israel’s election results be announced?

News channels will broadcast exit poll results once the election ends, with the first indications likely within a few hours of polls closing, but it could take days or weeks to get a clear result.

Results will also be live on the Central Elections Committee website once polls close.

While a clear picture of the election results may come out quickly, if no party or coalition secures a majority, it could take much longer.

The final vote tally is expected by Friday, and official election results are formally published a week after the election, on November 4.

Under a proportional representation system, Israelis vote for a single party, not individual candidates.

The number of seats the party gains in the Knesset is linked to the proportion of the vote it receives. For example, if Netanyahu’s Likud party secures 50 percent of the national vote, it would take 50 percent of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

A majority requires 61 of the 120 seats.

For a party to enter the Knesset, it must secure at least 3.25 percent of the national vote.

About a dozen parties are widely thought to have a chance of crossing the threshold, so the final tally and seat allocation will take time.

How is Israel’s next prime minister chosen?

Once the final count is in, President Isaac Herzog will speak with party leaders about who they want as prime minister, then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government.

The person nominated then has up to 42 days to form a government. As it stands, no single party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, so governments are formed by a coalition of parties, and negotiations on forming a government often take weeks.

What happens if Netanyahu or his rivals cannot form a government?

If no government emerges, the current cabinet, Netanyahu’s government, will remain as a caretaker government.

But before that point, whoever gains the most votes will have different options to assemble support from smaller parties, including forming a minority government or working with another political leader to alternate as prime minister under a power-sharing arrangement.

If all negotiations fail, and no grouping is able to cobble together a workable government, new elections will have to be called.

images.caption: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, leader of the Together (Beyachad) party, votes during the national election, in Raanana, Israel [Nir Elias/Reuters]
(Al Jazeera)

articles.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak tops 10,000 cases as authorities race to slow the spread in African countries
articles.summary: The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in Congo has reached 10,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Tuesday, as health authorities race to slow the spread of the disease in multiple African countries.
articles.body: The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in Congo has reached 10,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Tuesday, as health authorities race to slow the spread of the disease in multiple African countries. It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half of the 10,060 confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo’s Ministry of Health. That also makes it the deadliest outbreak of the disease in the country’s history. The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation. Those obstacles compound the challenge of persuading people to report symptoms and accept care in communities that have endured years of violence and repeated epidemics. Compared to the West Africa Ebola outbreak of 2014-2016 — history’s largest and deadliest with more than 28,000 cases, including over 11,000 deaths — this has had at least three times the number of cases and number of deaths in the time since it was declared. It has spread farther across Africa than any previous Ebola outbreak, reaching three regions with cases recorded in Kenya and Nigeria as well. It’s so far been recorded in five countries including Uganda and France, both of which have no active cases at the moment. A recurring problem in the spread in Africa is what appears to be lax surveillance efforts as most of the first cases were confirmed long after people started showing symptoms or after traveling. In Congo, the disease has spread to 66 health zones across eight provinces, from three zones when it was first declared in May. Responders have told The Associated Press that they’re seeing treatment centers in some of those health zones getting overwhelmed, people still skeptical and violent toward them, and health workers are regularly going on strike to protest delayed or unpaid wages. “Some people still don’t seem to understand the seriousness of the situation even though they are directly exposed to the risk,” said Sephora Bgosi with the Ebola burial team in Ituri province, the epicenter. “Ebola disease is extremely dangerous and can be deadly,” said Bgosi. About 80% of recorded cases are still coming from outside of monitored contacts, showing there are ongoing chains of transmission that health authorities are not aware of. At least 95% of recorded cases are supposed to be coming from known contacts for officials to say the outbreak has largely been brought under control, the Africa CDC has said. At least half of deaths recorded are among people who have not been admitted to treatment centers, a sign that people are still not reporting symptoms at all in many areas. In many zones, health workers are battling challenges ranging from basic needs such as adequate vehicles to complex ones like persuading families to release their relatives who are sick with the disease or who have died from it and need to be buried safely. Last week at the Nia Nia health zone in Ituri province, some Ebola responders, including surveillance and community engagement officers, went on strike over unpaid bonuses owed since late August, a common trend across many affected localities. More than five months since the outbreak was declared, health workers are still being attacked by angry villagers, including on Saturday when a nurse was killed and another health worker severely injured while responding to an Ebola alert in Bafwasende, Tshopo province. The outbreak has disrupted essential health services that are already underfunded and overstretched and has shifted attention away from other disease outbreaks the country is battling, such as cholera. More pregnant women are dying as they avoid hospitals over fear of infection and isolation, causing maternal mortality to double in some provinces soon after the outbreak was declared. It has also disrupted routine healthcare services such as childhood vaccinations, interrupted schooling for children where millions are already out of school, caused trauma and stigma for affected families and further stretched the livelihoods of many already struggling with hardship.

articles.title: 2 men charged with with helping Iran over incident at U.S.-run military base in Britain
articles.summary: LONDON — Two men were charged under the National Security Act on Tuesday over an incident last month at the RAF Fairford airbase, with prosecutors accusing a British national of trying to help Iranian intelligence in Britain.
articles.body: LONDON — Two men were charged under the National Security Act on Tuesday over an incident last month at the RAF Fairford airbase, with prosecutors accusing a British national of trying to help Iranian intelligence in Britain. RAF Fairford had been used by U.S. bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, but they were withdrawn on security grounds shortly after five British men were arrested outside the base in southwest England in the early hours of September 27. The circumstances of the incident, which remain largely unexplained, attracted huge international attention, coming at a time of heightened concern about the security implications for Western states of the war between the United States and Iran. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this month that the activity at RAF Fairford was likely to have been coordinated in Iran, which Tehran’s ambassador to Britain has denied. British national Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, was charged with engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service between August 31 and September 28, with police saying the country is believed to be Iran. Nouman Essghir, a 24-year-old dual British-Iranian national who was first arrested outside RAF Fairford on September 27, was charged with one offence of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on August 22. The pair will appear at London’s Westminster Magistrates’ Court later on Tuesday. Police said that six other people, four of whom are British nationals who were arrested outside RAF Fairford on September 27, remain on police bail. The decision to bail suspects after an apparent major incident had drawn scrutiny, but on Tuesday police said that decision had helped secure charges against the two men. “We know the decisions made during our investigations can sometimes appear illogical to those on the outside, but I want to make it very clear that there will always be a good reason or rationale behind them,” said Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the UK. “In this case, this decision-making has led to swifter progress, better evidence, and ultimately us securing the charges that I have announced today.”
