articles.title: The man behind some of your favorite scents
articles.summary: If you have worn Le Labo’s Santal 33 or Glossier’s You, you have experienced one of Frank Voelkl’s creations.
articles.body: Frank Voelkl is a well-dressed German man you’d walk past on your Manhattan commute without a second thought. But his work has likely been on your neck, your vanity, your partner or your ex. If you’ve worn fragrance in the last two decades, you’ve probably worn Voelkl. He is, arguably, the perfumer of the millennial olfactory oeuvre: Le Labo’s Santal 33, Glossier’s You, Phlur’s Father Figure, scents for Ariana Grande and Jennifer Lopez, work for Dolce & Gabbana, Calvin Klein and more. Voelkl is a master perfumer at DSM-Firmenich, one of the world’s leading fragrance houses — and is only the 16th in the company’s century-long history. It’s a rare distinction — there are more registered astronauts than master perfumers, who sit on the councils that choose which materials to pursue next, so you smell their predictions years later. “I would say we’re the ultimate experts,” Voelkl says, with exactly the right amount of modesty and fact. Voelkl’s perfumes are recognizable: clean but not sterile, woodsy but transparent, airy and modern without being clinical. The hugely popular “skin scent,” freshly washed skin remembered through a romantic haze, is practically defined by You and Father Figure. A bottle of You sells every 40 seconds, according to Glossier. Santal 33 turned creamy sandalwood into a sexy, mineralic fog. At its peak, whole blocks of Manhattan trailed its sillage. He likes almost everything he makes, but he wouldn’t wear all of it. His own taste runs to smokey, leathery materials, which he sneaks in at “very, very small, subliminal” doses. Any more, and, he finds, people read them as fire, danger, shadow. A clear vision — and nose Perfume is rarely given such airs outside of its own ecosystem – but the master perfumer designation creates a distinction the beauty world recognizes at a global scale. Masters advise the companies they work for on decisions both big and small. They sit on the councils that decide which materials to pursue next. You smell what they’ve predicted, years after they made their choices known. A master determines pathways to possible fragrant futures — and near ubiquity and instant smell-recognition is a hard skill to replicate. Voelkl has learned that success relies on the success of a workshop – a team of many voices, not just his own. “As a perfumer, we work with managers, evaluators, sales, marketing, the clients themselves. Our work is being edited. I see the evaluators as editors.” They often tell him a composition is too green or smokey to be commercial. “I listen to everybody and absorb the comments.” But it’s up to him, in the end, to decide which notes to take, and how to stay on the path to creation with the people who walk alongside him. He quotes a colleague’s advice often given to their trainees: “Don’t take the bus until you know where you’re going.” He explains his version as the following: “Hold a clear destination, stay open to a place nobody else has been, and accept the collaborators walking the road with you.” It is a matter of intuition and collective knowledge – and knowing when to listen to your own gut. “In the end, you’re alone. You’re alone as a creator, and you have to make that call.” The vanishing palette A perfumer’s raw materials are in a chaotic stage of both perpetual innovation and rapid disappearance. The industry is in the middle of a structural reformulation wave because of it. If you’ve noticed your longtime favorites being re-released recently — they’ve been swept up in this situation, and it’s been years in the making. From a chemist’s first search to the perfumer’s modification exploration, there are years and millions of dollars of research before the customer gets wind of anything happening. “You have to be five, ten years ahead — easily — in your thinking and in your strategy,” reflects Voelkl. Part of Voelkl’s job as a master and Senior Perfumer is to guide the research around the research and preservation of certain smells. Because certain natural fragrant materials are disappearing, and it happens more often than it has in past decades. Bay oil, for example, was wiped out almost entirely by Tropical Storm Erika and then Hurricane Maria hitting Dominica, where 70% of the global supply was produced. Natural disasters have devastated the distillery network. “Since then, we don’t have bay oil anymore,” Voelkl says, looking out the window. It is the material he misses most, and for a specific reason: “it smells like metal”, the only ingredient on his palette that did. He’s been searching for a replacement for years. A new old-spice-family material comes close, he says, but fragrance still on the market had to be quietly re-engineered around the absence. Other losses are regulatory. Fragrance compounds like Lilial and Lyral — “my fetish floral,” he calls the latter, a floral that lasts like a musk — are effectively off the table. One ingredient changing status sets off a chain reaction: Galaxolide, he predicts, will likely be gone from fragrance within five to ten years, another material in a veritable ocean of fragrance. “It’s another wave coming.” The wave never quite stops, and so the reinvention continues. Your favorite perfume, reinvented in ways you can smell but can’t quite spell out. Voelkl is there, lining the molecules up just so. You smell the success stories, but failure is inevitable While Voelkl’s work feels omnipresent in beauty stores likes Sephora and Ulta for his work with PHLUR, By Kilian, and Marc Jacobs – the smellscape of makeup shopping, really — if you ask him about his hit rate, he shrugs it off. “Statistically, I haven’t won that many briefs,” he deflects with a half-smile. “You’ll never know about the ones I didn’t win.” To date, he has more than 200 perfumes to his name. For context, there are entire years in which only 200 perfumes were ever released at all. The man is booked, even if rejections litter the laboratory floor. The wins make millions of dollars per perfume. “Sometimes those briefs are big, big projects you get very invested in. You do have to be emotionally involved to create. And sometimes they don’t go through, and you have to deal with that. It happens certainly more often than being chosen. You have to remove yourself emotionally,” says Voelkl. Like any artist seeking opportunities, rejection is part of the process. He has no batting average pinned to the wall and resists the idea that all briefs are equal. Some carry commercial weight, others the thrill of introducing a brand. There is, he admits, a private checklist. “I never did one for Yves Saint Laurent. I never did an Armani. I would love to,” he notes wistfully. In his head, there’s a Hall of Fame shelf with gaps in it, after more than 20 years of near ubiquity. For centuries, the perfumers behind the bottles were rarely listed anywhere to the public eye. Incredibly successful brands like INITIO and CREED still demur from divulging the perfumer’s they work with for their launches. The myth of the brand is paramount. But it’s becoming more of an industry norm for perfumers to not just be credited but treated as celebrities in and of themselves, their portraits shown alongside their finished work at events and unofficial merch is sold in their name on TikTok shop. Brands like Frederic Malle, Essential Parfums and the new brand Anecdote by Artists list the perfumers prominently alongside the name of the perfumes. Most of Voelkl’s work has been behind the curtain — known to the industry, not quite unlisted, but not front of bottle, either. But you can, in the end, create many successful perfumes and never be deemed a master of your field. What really leads to the title? Fragrance should leave a lasting impression. “You must be creating work that added to the map,” he explains. The second is character. “We are at the heart of it all.”

images.caption: As a master perfumer at DSM-Firmenich, Frank Voelkl is responsible for crafting signature scents that have gone on to define the millennial perfume palette.
According to Glossier, a bottle of You — its signature, bestselling fragrance developed by Voelkl — sells every forty seconds.
At one point, customers flocked to get their hands on Le Labo's Santal 33 perfume — first via a spritz of the famed fragrance, and then later via soaps, lotions, and candles.

articles.title: Why Jordan has struck Syria: What we know
articles.summary: Syria says Jordan did not coordinate with Damascus before launching operation in rural Deraa and Suwayda.
articles.body:
Jordan said its air force conducted retaliatory attacks on what it called “dens of terrorist organizations in southern Syria”, linked to suspects accused of being behind last week’s attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the kingdom.

In a post on X, the Jordanian Armed Forces said: “Fighter jets from the Royal Air Force destroyed a number of terrorist sites in southeastern Syria.

“The operation resulted in the killing and wounding of many elements of the terrorist organizations and the destruction of a number of their vehicles,” Jordan’s Armed Forces added.

“The armed forces said the operation was conducted in coordination with ⁠Damascus.” Jordan’s military said in a further post on X.

ISIL (ISIS) has claimed responsibility for the October 23 church attack.

Jordan did not specify the locations of the attacks or provide casualty figures.

Syria has contradicted Jordan’s account of the overnight attacks.

In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs informed Jordan of its “complete reservation” over the attacks, which took place “without prior coordination or notification with the Syrian side”.

A Foreign Ministry official told Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett that the strikes were a “treacherous attack”.

Pett reported from Syria that authorities have said seven people were killed, including three children, in Jordanian air attacks on Deraa and Suwayda countryside.

Syria’s Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management said its teams had responded to attacks in four sites.

Syria’s civil defence agency said it had recovered the bodies of those killed in attacks. They include five members of one family, including three children and a woman who were killed together in a strike on a tent in the village of al-Taff, in the Lajat area of northeastern Deraa province. Three other members of the family were injured, it said.

In the al-Shayah farms near Nassib, in Deraa countryside, a strike on a farm killed Riyad Karrad, 80. His body was taken to Deraa National Hospital.

In Muzayrib, in the Ein al-Basal area of western Deraa countryside, a strike hit a home. No casualties were reported.

In the town of Shuhayb, in northern Suwayda countryside, a strike on a home killed Mutlaq Abu al-Khail, 60. Rescue teams were still working to recover his body from the rubble when the report was issued.

There was no immediate comment from Jordan on Syria’s accusations that civilians – not armed fighters – were killed.

Shortly after the attacks, Syrian customs authorities on Tuesday closed the Nassib border crossing with Jordan, the only passenger and commercial traffic pathway between the neighbours.

Jordan said its attacks on Syrian territory were in response to an attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.

On Monday, senior government security officials said Jordanian security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law after a shootout over the violence that killed nine people in a rare attack on the minority Christian community in Jordan on Friday.

Major-General Obaidullah al-Maaytah, Jordan’s director of public security, named the three detained suspects as Hazza Zaidan Mohammed, Meshal Zaidan Mohammed and Ahmad Sami Hussein.

The attack during a funeral prompted Jordan’s King Abdullah II to order security forces to respond with an “iron fist”.

Jordan’s Interior Minister Mazin al-Farrayeh said he was launching an investigation “examining all the circumstances that lead young people towards extremism”.

“The file has not yet been closed; investigations are still ongoing. As of today, there are ⁠no indications of any links between them and other cells,” al-Farrayeh added.

Has Jordan struck Syrian territory in the past?

Jordan has conducted multiple air attacks on Syria since 2023, saying it was targeting drug and arms smugglers.

The operations have sometimes hit civilians.

Human Rights Watch demanded accountability after Jordan launched attacks that killed women and children in January 2024.

“Cross-border airstrikes that kill civilians demand scrutiny regardless of the threat posed by drug smuggling from southern Syria,” Human Rights Watch said.

The Jordanian Armed Forces said its operations along its border were aimed at armed groups reportedly carrying narcotics, arms, and explosives that it suspected are linked to Iran-allied groups.

How will Syria respond to Jordan’s latest attack?

Syria’s Foreign Ministry said it was in contact with Jordan to establish the circumstances of the operation.

Damascus said it will address the aftermath of the attacks while “safeguarding Syria’s security and sovereignty”.

articles.title: Speaker Johnson predicts Democrats' far-left shift will ‘juice enthusiasm’ for GOP in midterms
articles.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson claims polls grossly underestimate Republican enthusiasm, warning the Democratic Party has taken a dangerous lurch left.
articles.body: With the midterm elections just a week away, House Speaker Mike Johnson warned that GOP voter enthusiasm should not be underestimated, and the Democratic Party’s increasingly left-wing agenda will drive Americans toward Republicans, despite polls showing Democrats with a national advantage. "If these Democrats took control of Congress, it would be crazier than the Obama years and the Biden-Harris years, because they've taken a far lurch to the left," he said on "The Ingraham Angle" Monday. "And people see that, and I think it's going to juice enthusiasm for our side." Johnson decried the policy stances of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), which several prominent midterm congressional candidates have affiliated themselves with. He warned that their proposals to abolish borders and prisons and defund police departments would be dangerous for the country. SOCIALIST VICTORIES SHOW DEMS' DESCENT DOWN 'DEADLY PATH OF COMMUNISM,' JOHNSON WARNS "This is not our father's Democrat Party," the speaker said. "This group is taking a far turn to the left. You see it by their all-star candidates they're promoting around the country." Johnson characterized the 2026 midterms as a "contrast election," saying voters face a choice between "common sense" and "crazy." ANTI-SOCIALISM PUSH CAN FLIP BATTLEGROUNDS, REPUBLICAN LEADER BETS AS PARTY FIGHTS TO HOLD HOUSE "Truly, everybody has to ask themselves the simple question: Which set of policies is better for my family, my aging parents, my children? You have to vote Republican," he said. "You would be turning the keys over to a group of angry Democrats, who are going to go after retribution of President Trump and his administration. They're going to open those borders wide. They're gonna try to repeal the working families tax cut and all that we've done in the economy." Johnson’s comments come as polls show Democrats leading Republicans this midterm election cycle. A new Reuters Ipsos poll found that registered voters favored Democrats over Republicans by 47% to 36%. The House leader argued that polls are misrepresentative and underestimate Republican enthusiasm. He claimed that Republican voters have become increasingly unwilling to participate in polls and surveys because of distrust. LEE CARTER: POLLS SAY DEMOCRATS COULD SWAMP REPUBLICANS. AS A POLLSTER, I HAVE A QUESTION "The polls are grossly underestimating Republican enthusiasm around the country," he told Fox News host Laura Ingraham. articles.title: When is Karwa Chauth in 2026? Story, History, Significance, Importance, and all you need to know
articles.summary: The festival season is here, and the air already smells of winter's arrival.
articles.body: The festival season is here, and the air already smells of winter's arrival. It is that time of the year when fairy lights deck up homes, music fills the streets, and colourful trinkets, flowers, and bandhanwars line the markets.Many festivals line this season every year, and the upcoming one is Karwachauth, when married women break their day-long water fast after the first glimpse of their husbands.Across North India, homes begin to hum with preparation days earlier. Markets fill with bangles, colourful dupattas and decorated clay pots. Hands are adorned with mehndi, and phone calls go back and forth between sisters, mothers and friends, all asking the same thing: what time will the moon come out this year?Let's read further to know more about the festival and when Karwa Chauth is in 2026.Date and pooja tithi of Karwa Chauth 2026Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, 29 October 2026, this year according to Drikpanchang, the Chaturthi tithi starts at 1:06 AM on 29 October and ends at 10:09 PM that night, so the vrat is kept on 29 October across India.The reason behind this is that Chaturthi must be present when the moon rises, because the fast ends with Chandra puja.Karwachauth 2026 puja muhurat, fasting hours and moonriseAccording to Drik Panchang:Fast begins: 6:31 AM (sunrise)Puja muhurat: 5:38 PM to 6:56 PM (1 hour 17 minutes)Moonrise: around 8:17 PMWho is worshipped on Karwachauth?Karva Mata, a form of Goddess Parvati linked with marital bliss, is worshipped with Lord Shiva, along with Ganesha and Kartikeya. Chaturthi is Ganesha's tithi, so he is the first one to be prayed to, and then the final arghya is given to the moon.Chandra rules the mind, emotions, and the bond of care between two people. Moon worship on this day is meant to bring peace into married life and protect the husband's health and long life.Legend behind Karwachauth: The story of VeeravatiThere is an age-old mythological legend behind the celebration of Karwachauth surrounding Veeravati, who was the only sister of seven brothers, and they adored her. After her marriage, she came to her parents' home for her first Karwa Chauth. She fasted without food or water, and by evening hunger and thirst made her faint.Her brothers could not bear to see her suffer. They lit a fire behind a peepal tree and held a sieve in front of it, so the glow looked like the rising moon. Veervati believed them, offered arghya to the false moon and ate. Soon after, news came that her husband had died.Heartbroken, she sat beside his body for a year, praying without pause. Goddess Parvati told her the fast had been broken before the real moonrise. She advised Veervati to keep every Chaturthi vrat that year and to observe the next Karwa Chauth with complete faith. Veervati did, and her husband's life was restored. The story is that the fast is complete only when the real moon is seen.How is the festival celebrated?Traditionally, women keep the fast for the long life of their husbands. It is a nirjala fast, with no food or water from sunrise to moonrise. In the present day, husbands also join in, couples celebrate equality, and Over the years, rituals and festivals like this have helped strengthen social bonds among women, including with in-laws and friends.What rituals are followed during KarwachauthHere is the complete fasting guideBefore dawn: Wake up early and have the sargi your mother-in-law sends. It usually has dry fruits, pheni or kheer, fresh fruits, and mathri. Drink plenty of water at this time, since most women don't have any during the day.Through the day: Take it easy, avoid heavy work and long trips, and rest in the afternoon if you can. Many women put on mehendi a day earlier. On the evening of the vrat, they dress in red, maroon or other bridal colours. Solah shringar is traditional, but a simple, neat outfit is just as good.Getting the puja ready: Set up your thali with roli, rice, a diya, sweets, a karwa filled with water, and a chalni (sieve). Place a picture of Karva Mata on the wall or on a wooden plank, or draw one.At the puja time: Light the lamp and pray to Ganesha first. Then pray to Karva Mata, along with Shiva and Parvati, and listen to the katha. If you are sitting in a group, you can pass your thalis around seven times while singing traditional songs.When the moon rises, look at the moon through the chalni and offer water from the karwa. Then look at your husband through the same chalni. He gives you your first sip of water and a sweet, and that concludes the fast. Follow it with a light dinner, since a heavy meal on an empty stomach can upset you.FAQs (Frequently asked questions)1. When is Karwa Chauth in 2026?Thursday, 29 October 2026 in India.2. What are the puja muhurat and moonrise timings in Delhi?The puja muhurat is 5:38 PM to 6:56 PM, and moonrise is around 8:17 PM.3. Who is worshipped on Karwa Chauth?Karva Mata, Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha and Kartikeya are worshipped, with the moon receiving the final arghya.4. Why do women look at the moon through a sieve?It is a traditional custom: women view the moon and then their husband through the sieve before the fast is broken.5. Can pregnant women or people with health conditions keep the fast?They should not keep a waterless fast, and may take fruits, milk or water after speaking to a doctor.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Scotland's recycling rates fall to lowest level in five years
articles.summary: Environmental regulator Sepa says households recycled 42.8% of waste in 2025 - down from 44.3% the previous year.
articles.body:
Scotland's recycling rate has fallen to its lowest level in five years, according to figures from the Scottish Environment Protection Agency (Sepa).

The Scottish government's environmental regulator says households recycled 42.8% of waste in 2025 - down from 44.3% the previous year.

According to a roadmap set by the Scottish government in 2010, recycling rates should have hit 70% last year but are falling well short.

The share of waste processed at an incinerator remained broadly the same at 82% but the amount being diverted to landfill fell by 10%.

Recycling rates vary massively by local authority. South Ayrshire's residents recycled 55% of their waste, compared to 26% in Glasgow.

The islands have the lowest rates, with Orkney recording a figure of just 18.2%.

A total of 2.31 million tonnes of waste was created by households in 2025, which represents a fall of just 1,500 tonnes.

Recycling rates have remained similar - at about 45% - for more than a decade.

The biggest change has been seen in the way black bag waste is treated.

A rapid growth in the construction of energy-from-waste plants, which generate electricity by burning rubbish, has seen a shift away from landfill.

But this has not happened quickly enough to meet a landfill ban which was due to come in at the start of the year. It has now been effectively delayed to 2028.

The figures do not reflect a disruption to Scotland's waste management by the long-term repairs being carried out to the incinerator at Polmadie in Glasgow.

The Glasgow Recycling and Renewable Energy Centre in Glasgow was shut down in April this year, with much of the waste being diverted to other incinerators or landfill.

The centre is operated, along with a facility at Dunbar, by Viridor.

Karen MacCormick from the company says waste incineration is a greener option than landfill because it can also generate electricity.

She added: "When it's in landfill you've got the landfill gasses, you've got methane, etc.

"This is a more sustainable way of dealing with the waste, coming through an energy recovery facility, and obviously we can create something at the end of it which is low carbon energy going straight to the grid."

A deposit return scheme for bottles and cans, which has seen recycling rates increase significantly in other countries, has been repeatedly delayed .

Experts have also suggested that the lack of consistency in what is collected by local authorities across the country makes it confusing for households.

While some councils take glass at the kerbside, for example, others are forced to drop them off at bottle banks.

Research from Zero Waste Scotland also suggests that more than half of the waste placed in black bins could be recycled.

Sepa's chief scientific officer, Dr Richard Allan, says the figures highlight an "ongoing challenge" with how waste is managed.

He added: "It's clear that where waste ends up is important, but we need to focus on preventing waste in the first place and recycling more of that material when it is produced."

Waste sector crisis could see rubbish piling up on streets, experts warn

Truckloads of Scotland's rubbish will be sent to England, experts say

Sabotage, betrayal, secrecy... and recycling

Kim Pratt, senior circular economy campaigner at Friends of the Earth Scotland, said there had been a "shocking decline" in recycling rates.

She said this showed that Scotland had "lost its way", with households missing the 2025 target of 70% recycling "by a mile".

"Recycling levels have stalled in Scotland since the Scottish government encouraged a new generation of waste incinerators to be built, meaning that household waste which could have been recycled is being burned instead," she said.

"The Scottish government is expected to consult on new circular economy targets this year.

"If these are to be meaningful, it must learn the lessons from the past – setting targets is the easy part, meeting them requires real commitment and planning that puts people and nature first."

The Scottish government has been approached for comment.

articles.title: A Pennsylvania tire-shop worker turned discarded rubber into a prize-winning parade lion, then built an eight-foot, 700-pound fire-breathing dragon that won first prize and became a roadside attraction
articles.summary: Along a Pennsylvania roadside, an ordinary tire shop has become an unlikely gallery of giant creatures.
articles.body: Along a Pennsylvania roadside, an ordinary tire shop has become an unlikely gallery of giant creatures. What began as a parade project has grown into a collection of fantastical sculptures made from discarded rubber, metal and salvaged materials. At the centre of it all is Noah Russell, a young tire-shop worker whose imagination has transformed old tyres into a prize-winning lion, a fire-breathing dragon and an increasingly popular roadside attraction in Littlestown.From tyre shop to creative workshopRussell works at Breighner’s Tire Center, where owner Randy Breighner first noticed his ability to turn used tyres into something far more imaginative. According to Atlas Obscura, Breighner challenged Russell to create a float for Littlestown’s annual Good Ole Days Festival parade.The result was a lion constructed largely from tyres. According to Atlas Obscura and Wavy News, the creation won first place, giving Russell an unusual platform for what would become a continuing artistic experiment. The following year, he decided that another parade entry needed to be considerably more ambitious. The lion was replaced by an eight-foot-tall dragon made from vulcanized rubber and other repurposed materials.Building a dragon from discarded rubberAs per Wavy News, the dragon's construction relied heavily on materials Russell encountered through his work at the tyre centre. Turf tyres, commonly used on lawn equipment, became the primary material for the body because they could be cut and shaped relatively easily. Their tread patterns also created a naturally scaly appearance.Metal formed the foundation of the wings, while coat hangers helped shape and support them. Russell also saved classic whitewall tyres that had come into the shop, eventually transforming them into the dragon's teeth and horns.The result was a sculpture that turned a familiar waste material into something theatrical and almost mythical.The creature that breathes fireThe dragon's most dramatic feature is its ability to produce real flames. According to Wavy News, a motor pushes butane through a long brake line, while a remotely operated heated coil ignites the gas.The mechanical system gives the sculpture its signature fire-breathing effect, turning an already imposing roadside installation into something that commands attention.Atlas Obscura notes that the dragon went on to win first place at the Good Ole Days Festival parade, giving Russell consecutive victories. Its popularity soon carried beyond Littlestown, with the creation appearing in Halloween parades in Gettysburg and Hanover.A roadside menagerie takes shapeRussell's creativity did not stop with the lion and dragon. He later constructed an elaborate headless horseman sculpture, although the parade where it was intended to appear was cancelled during the COVID-19 pandemic.Instead, the horseman joined the lion and dragon at the tyre shop. According to Atlas Obscura, the three sculptures became a source of entertainment and community spirit during the pandemic.Over time, the collection expanded further, adding a horned stag and a reef populated with aquatic creatures. WGAL News and Atlas Obscura have covered how the tire center on Hanover Pike's odd displays have become a local landmark.What began with a request for a parade float has ultimately transformed a working tire shop into an open-air showcase of creative recycling, where discarded rubber finds an unexpected second life as fantastical art.Images Courtesy: istock and Atlas ObscuraYou use AI every day. articles.title: In 2023, Nina Dobrev and Shaun White bought a $4.3 million Hollywood Hills home and began renovating it; after their engagement ended in 2025, the house was reportedly offered for rent at $35,000 a month
articles.summary: Nina Dobrev and Shaun White’s Hollywood Hills home became one of the most talked-about celebrity real estate stories of 2025, not because of its price
articles.body: Nina Dobrev and Shaun White’s Hollywood Hills home became one of the most talked-about celebrity real estate stories of 2025, not because of its price alone, but because of what it represented. The couple bought the $4.3 million midcentury modern property in 2023, began renovating it as their shared Los Angeles (LA) base, and later put it on the rental market for roughly $35,000 a month after ending their engagement. Architectural Digest reported the purchase and design details, while SFGate and US Weekly later connected the property to the former couple’s separation.The house was more than a luxury address. For Dobrev and White, it appeared to be the first home they purchased together, a place where they could merge their lives after years of dating and travelling together. When news of their split emerged in September 2025, attention naturally turned to the property, its renovation, and the question of what would happen to a home that had once seemed intended for a future together.A $4.3 million Hollywood Hills purchaseDobrev, best known for 'The Vampire Diaries', and White, the three-time Olympic snowboarding champion, bought the Hollywood Hills home in July 2023 for $4.3 million, according to Architectural Digest. The property was built in 1964 and sits on 0.38 acres in a hillside setting, with trees and hedges providing privacy around the residence.The home was described as a midcentury modern estate with a small pool house and views toward the mountains and the city below. Architectural Digest reported that it had four bedrooms and five bathrooms, along with an open-plan main level connecting the kitchen, dining area, and living space. Sliding glass doors opened to a balcony and pool area, while the outdoor space also included a bocce ball court on a terraced level below the house.SFGate later described the residence as 3,793 square feet, with four bedrooms and four bathrooms, a two-car garage, an infinity pool, tropical landscaping, and a bocce court. The listing details varied slightly between reports, but both accounts presented the home as a stylish, view-oriented property designed for indoor-outdoor living.A renovation project and a shared futureAt the time of the purchase, the home was not simply a finished celebrity mansion waiting to be moved into. US Weekly reported that the property was under renovation when Dobrev and White separated in 2025, suggesting that the couple had been actively shaping it into a shared home. For the unversed, Dobrev and White had been together since around 2019 or 2020, and so their Hollywood Hills house appeared to be part of their life together. SFGate noted that many people believed the property would become their marital home after White proposed to Dobrev in October 2024.The engagement itself had been widely covered. White proposed with a five-carat diamond ring by Lorraine Schwartz during a surprise dinner at The Golden Swan in New York City, according to US Weekly. Dobrev shared the moment on Instagram with the caption, “RIP boyfriend, hello fiancé,” making the relationship milestone public and adding to the sense that the couple was building a future together.The split changed the plansIn September 2025, reports confirmed that Dobrev and White had ended their engagement and relationship after about five years together. PEOPLE first reported the news, and a source described the decision as mutual, difficult, and made with love and respect.US Weekly later reported that the two remained in contact because parts of their lives were still intertwined, including the home they shared. A source said they were working out “next steps” for the property, which was still being renovated at the time. The outlet also reported that neither infidelity nor disagreement over having children was the reason for the breakup; instead, the former couple had simply grown apart.The timing made the house especially poignant. Less than two weeks before the split became public, Dobrev and White had been photographed holding hands at a Los Angeles farmers market. Soon after, Dobrev attended a red carpet event without her engagement ring, and she later unpinned her engagement photos from Instagram, signs that fuelled speculation before the separation was confirmed.Listed for nearly $35,000 a monthThe most striking real estate development came in February 2025, when property records indicated that the Hollywood Hills home was offered for rent at $34,995 per month, according to SFGate. The listing was removed days later, and records suggested that the property had been leased.That monthly figure placed the home firmly in Los Angeles’ ultra-luxury rental market. At nearly $35,000 a month, the annual rent would amount to more than $419,000, a sum that reflects both the property’s location and its high-end features. For a home bought for $4.3 million, renting it out also offered a practical way to keep the asset occupied and generating income while the former couple decided what to do next.It is not clear from the available reports who leased the property or whether either Dobrev or White intended to retain it long term. SFGate reported that ownership remained unclear after the split, while US Weekly said the two were still finalising details related to the home.What the house says about celebrity real estateCelebrity homes often attract attention because they offer a glimpse into a famous couple’s private life, but the Dobrev and White property became newsworthy for a different reason. It showed how real estate can become part of a relationship’s public narrative, especially when a couple buys, renovates, and later rents out a home within a short period.The Hollywood Hills house also highlighted the practical side of celebrity property ownership. Both Dobrev and White already owned other homes: Architectural Digest reported that Dobrev still had her Spanish-style West Hollywood residence, while White owned properties including a Nevada ranch, a Malibu estate, and a Utah cabin.For now, the $4.3 million home remains a reminder of a chapter that changed. It began as a joint purchase and renovation project for a couple planning a life together, then became a high-value rental listing after their engagement ended. The house’s next owners or tenants may see only a beautifully designed Los Angeles property, but its recent history gives it a story that extends well beyond its views, pool, and midcentury architecture.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Jalen Hurts' blood clot case will 'put the league on alert' going forward, famed agent Leigh Steinberg says
articles.summary: Leigh Steinberg says Jalen Hurts' blood clot case will put the NFL on alert and raises questions about whether the Eagles should have cleared him to play.
articles.body: Legendary NFL agent Leigh Steinberg weighed in on the handling of Jalen Hurts' recent blood clot situation, and predicted the impact it may have on the league and quarterback agents moving forward. Steinberg said he would have contacted team doctors and sought answers if a quarterback he represented faced a similar situation. He predicted Hurts’ case would put the league on alert, while repeatedly emphasizing that medical experts must determine whether the Eagles handled his care appropriately. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "The words ‘blood clot’ would set off an alarm bell in my head," he told OutKick. "I would have certainly been in touch with the Philadelphia medical staff, with the Eagles medical staff, and asked questions because blood clot is a red flag." Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season after further testing revealed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli — blood clots affecting both lungs. The NFL and NFL Players Association announced Oct. 25 that they were working together to review the matter, following the union’s demand for an investigation. JALEN HURTS BLOOD CLOT INVESTIGATION TO RAISE QUESTIONS ABOUT EAGLES' LONDON TRIP AND MEDICAL SCREENING TIMING For Steinberg, the situation illustrates why an agent’s responsibilities must extend beyond negotiating contracts. "This just highlights the active role that every agent has to play in safeguarding the health both short term and long term," he said. "It’s where you have to put football aside for a moment," he added, "and the pressures of a season." Steinberg also expressed confidence in Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, and said his description of how he would respond should not be interpreted as an accusation that she failed her client. "I believe that his agent was diligent," he said. "I know his agent, she’s excellent." The scrutiny centers on Hurts being cleared to play against Jacksonville in London on Oct. 11 after an ultrasound identified a superficial clot in his left calf. According to the Eagles, Hurts first sought treatment Oct. 8, telling medical personnel he had been cleated during the Oct. 4 game against the Rams. He practiced fully before traveling to London, where the ultrasound was performed Oct. 10. The team said its medical staff and London doctors determined that activity and mobility were important and that he could safely play. After Hurts returned to Philadelphia, a follow-up ultrasound Oct. 14 revealed movement in the clot, the Eagles said. He was subsequently placed on injured reserve Oct. 17. FORMER NFL TEAM DOCTOR ADDRESSES JALEN HURTS' BLOOD CLOT AS QB'S SEASON HINGES ON ONE KEY WORD "Should he have played in London?" Steinberg asked. "That’s an open question." He stressed that the later diagnosis alone does not establish that the earlier medical decisions were wrong. "This is a medical question which can only be analyzed by experts in the field of blood clot diagnosis," he said. Steinberg said he knows Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie and general manager Howie Roseman and believes they are committed to player health. He raised the possibility that Hurts’ condition continued developing despite appropriate attention, and said he knew of no evidence establishing that the diagnosis should have been handled differently. The NFL has defended the care Hurts received. "I have complete confidence in the Eagles’ medical staff and their handling of this situation," NFL medical chief Allen Sills said. The NFLPA, however, called for a full investigation before conclusions are reached. Front Office Sports reported Oct. 25 that the league and union were discussing the investigation’s process and details, citing a source who said it had not formally launched. Hurts’ diagnosis is serious, but the Eagles and Lynn have described him as clinically stable, with no significant functional limitations, and said they expect a full recovery without long-term effects. His treatment involves blood thinners, and he cannot participate in contact activities while taking them. Their statement said he could remain around the team and continue conditioning. Superficial vein thrombosis affects veins near the skin’s surface and is generally less dangerous than deep vein thrombosis. A deep-vein clot can break off and travel to the lungs, causing a potentially life-threatening pulmonary embolism. The distinction matters when assessing what doctors knew at each stage of Hurts’ care. Steinberg expects the case to encourage greater caution across football. "The progression of this from a marginal health problem to a potential life-threatening problem is going to put the league on alert," he said. Asked whether other agents were discussing the situation, he stopped short of identifying specific conversations. "I think they should be," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Steinberg connected that responsibility to his work on concussions and brain health, including his foundation and medical conferences. His foundation focuses on understanding, preventing and treating concussions, traumatic brain injuries and related conditions. He said he came to view protecting players’ immediate and future health as a fiduciary responsibility. The football consequences are substantial, too. articles.title: An Indiana candidate asked a judge to force an election commission meeting before November 3 over complaints, including a disputed $60,000 campaign contribution; the judge refused, delaying review until after voting
articles.summary: A judge in Indiana has ruled that the state’s Election Commission is not required to consider campaign finance complaints against two secretary of state
articles.body: A judge in Indiana has ruled that the state’s Election Commission is not required to consider campaign finance complaints against two secretary of state candidates before the November 3 election, rejecting a legal bid to force an early hearing.Marion County Superior Court Judge Jennifer Harrison on Monday denied a request by Lincoln Party candidate Greg Ballard, who had sought an order compelling the commission to meet before Election Day to examine allegations against Republican Max Engling and Democrat Beau Bayh.The commission is scheduled to take up the complaints at its November 20 meeting, after voters have cast their ballots.Harrison said Ballard had failed to show that delaying the hearing would cause him concrete harm. She also questioned his argument that an earlier meeting would affect voters’ decisions in the secretary of state race.“He instead presents hypothetical harm with no support that if Defendants meet before November 3, it will affect voter decision-making in the Secretary of State race,” Harrison wrote in her decision, as reported by the Indiana Capital Chronicle.Judge cites lack of evidence of harmBallard had argued that voters should have an opportunity to learn about the campaign finance allegations against his opponents before voting. His legal challenge sought to compel the commission to consider the complaints before the election.The state attorney general’s office opposed the request, arguing during a court hearing on Friday that state law does not specify a deadline for the commission to review campaign finance complaints. It also accused Ballard of trying to use the commission to influence voters before Election Day.In her ruling, Harrison said Ballard had not established any concrete harm arising from the commission’s decision to wait until its scheduled meeting.Ballard criticised the decision in a statement, saying the law was failing to protect voters from political manoeuvring.“Might makes right. The laws are intended to protect those in power,” he said, adding that he was exploring legal options to compel the commission to fulfil what he described as its statutory duty to meet.$60,000 donation at centre of complaintOne of the most prominent complaints concerns an alleged $60,000 campaign contribution received by Engling’s campaign from Hoosier Leadership for America, a political group associated with Republican US Senator Jim Banks.The complaint, filed in July by Knox County Clerk David Shelton, alleged that the contribution was improperly accepted. Shelton had finished second to Engling in the contest for the Republican nomination at the state party convention in June.Engling’s campaign has said it returned the money about a week before the complaint was filed.Other pending complaints concern Bayh, with allegations that he attended several events sponsored by county Democratic parties but did not report in-kind contributions from those organisations.Republican Shelton has also joined Ballard’s legal challenge. He has argued that the return of the $60,000 contribution does not eliminate the need for a hearing examining the source of the money.Commission yet to take up complaintsIndiana’s Election Commission has two Republican and two Democratic members. Its chair, Beth Boyce, who also serves as the Republican chair in Johnson County, has the authority to call meetings of the panel.The commission is currently scheduled to consider the pending complaints on November 20, more than two weeks after Election Day on November 3.The ruling means the commission will not be compelled by Ballard’s lawsuit to convene before voters choose the next secretary of state. articles.title: Mao, memes and Mbappé: Chinese brands drop soccer star in fury over ‘dictator’ joke
articles.summary: He’s one of the world’s most popular athletes, but Kylian Mbappé is suddenly paying the penalty for being on the wrong side of China’s fervent nationalism.
articles.body: HONG KONG — He’s one of the world’s most popular athletes, but Kylian Mbappé is suddenly paying the penalty for being on the wrong side of China’s fervent nationalism. The French soccer star’s own goal? Suggesting that Mao Zedong, the founding leader of communist China, was a dictator, in comments that revolved around memes portraying Mbappé as an authoritarian figure. A host of Chinese brands said Tuesday that they were cutting ties with the French captain, the latest example of how rapidly celebrities can go from having their faces plastered in subway stations and on drink bottles to drawing condemnation over political sensitivities that are little understood outside China. The scale of the backlash prompted La Liga, the Spanish league of which Mbappé is the leading light, to apologize and distance itself from his remarks. Mbappé himself then apologized “to everyone my words have upset,” saying that his “comment was ill-judged.” The swift apologies aimed to head off what had been a wave of outrage. Dongpeng Beverage, known for its energy drinks, Inner Mongolia Mengniu Dairy, one of China’s largest dairy producers, and cheesemaker Milkground all issued similarly worded statements early Tuesday announcing that they were terminating their ties with Mbappé. The Chinese social media platform Xiaohongshu also distanced itself from Mbappé, saying its contract with him had ended after he appeared in a 2024 ad for the platform that went viral. On Tuesday, a note on Mbappé’s Xiaohongshu account, which had more than a million followers, said it had been suspended “for violating community guidelines.” The companies did not specify Mbappé’s missteps, but the statements came after a clip circulated widely on social media Monday showing an interview last spring with the French online talk show “The Bridge.” Mbappé is often depicted jokingly online as a dictator because of his outsize presence on and off the field. Fans have created memes comparing him to a number of authoritarian historical figures, including Mao. In the clip, Mbappé was asked which meme was his favorite. “A video someone made of a guy… I think he was a Chinese dictator,” he said. The clip then shows Mbappé’s face superimposed on an image of Mao, whom Mbappé did not mention by name. His comments drew fury in China, where he was accused of insulting a country that has been a lucrative source of income for him. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with a collective boycott by all sectors of Chinese society,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Tuesday at a regular briefing in Beijing. Foreign athletes have run afoul of Chinese sensitivities in the past, sometimes with profound economic consequences for major sports leagues. NBA games were largely suspended from Chinese broadcast for years in 2019 after a Houston Rockets manager expressed support for anti-government protests in the Chinese territory of Hong Kong, and in 2023 former NBA star Dwight Howard drew controversy when he referred to the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan as a country. According to a commentary Tuesday by Global Times, a state-backed nationalist tabloid, sporting events and advertisements involving Mbappé have also been suspended from broadcasting. “Mbappé is not an isolated case. He has now paid the price, and deservedly so,” the commentary said. “His experience should serve as a clear red line for all foreign public figures seeking to enter the Chinese market.” After reports that broadcasts of the Spanish league, where Mbappé plays for Real Madrid, had been suspended in China, the league distanced itself from the remarks. “We deeply regret” the comments “that have caused discomfort and offense in China,” La Liga President Javier Tebas said in a post on social media. “We cannot allow an individual’s action to tarnish” La Liga and its clubs’ relationship with China, Tebas said, adding that it was working with its partners in China to “overcome the situation.” In his own apology, also posted to social media, Mbappé said that “during a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself. My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.” He added: “I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.” Mbappé came a close second Monday for soccer’s prestigious Ballon d’Or award. He has criticized the dictator memes in the past, telling the French sports newspaper L’Équipe last month that while he knew they were meant to be humorous, they also showed “a lack of political and human awareness.” Mao has a deeply mixed legacy in China, which he led for more than a quarter-century until his death in 1976. In 1949, Mao’s communist forces won China’s drawn-out civil war, unifying the country after a century of foreign invasion and domestic turmoil. In the decades that followed, Mao oversaw sweeping reforms that included the “Great Leap Forward” — a radical industrialization campaign that contributed to famines that are believed to have killed tens of millions of people — as well as the “Cultural Revolution,” a violent anti-capitalist movement that stirred political and social chaos for the last decade of his rule. China’s ruling Communist Party has acknowledged Mao’s role in those events but maintains that his achievements outweigh his mistakes. His stature within the party remains high, and his portrait appears on the 100-yuan bill, the largest denomination of Chinese currency. Mao also continues to be a source of inspiration for some young people frustrated by China’s slowing economy and fiercely competitive society, and Mbappé’s comments drew online criticism. Many didn’t know what exactly Mbappé had said, however, given China’s strict censorship controls.“I don’t care what exactly he said. If it was insulting to China, then it hurt my feelings. I support boycotting him,” read one comment on Weibo. Mark Dreyer, author of a book on China’s sports industry, said the episode was the latest involving China in which a story fuels outrage that forces brands to take action to protect commercial interests no matter the context or truth. “The ultimate result is that sports stars and global celebrities will become increasingly cautious about engaging with China,” Dreyer said. “It’s hard to see how this outcome benefits China or its sports fans in the long run.”

articles.title: Shrewsbury first-time buyer wary of Budget housing loan scheme
articles.summary: Luke Anstee has been saving for three years but says rising living costs make home ownership harder.
articles.body:
For Luke Anstee, buying a first home would mean more than getting on the property ladder.

The 23-year-old hopes it would give him the chance to put down roots after spending much of his childhood moving around because of his father's Army career.

Further details of the government's proposed Your First Home scheme are expected in Wednesday's Budget, with ministers saying it could help first-time buyers purchase a property with a deposit as low as 2.5%.

Anstee said he had rarely lived in one place for long.

"I don't think I've ever stayed in one place for more than three years at a time, so it would be nice to actually have somewhere where I can stay," he said.

Having spent 10 years in Germany and moving around the UK, he said he was craving stability and the opportunity to buy a place of his own.

Despite saving money every month for the past three years, he believes home ownership is still some way off.

"It is not where I would like it to be. When I can, I try and put more in, but one of the things I am mindful of is that I am in my final year of university," he said.

"I am over the threshold of when I have to start paying [my student loan] back."

Anstee earns more than £25,000 a year working in IT and lives in a house share.

However, he said the cost of living makes it harder to save.

"If you think about my weekly shop, back in the day that would probably be £20-30. Now it's £60," he said.

"I used to pay high 40s, low 50s [to fill up on petrol]. Now I pay nearly £70 a tank.

"You can cut back on subscriptions and stuff but I don't pay for any."

What is the Budget and what could be in it?

Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme

Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder

The government announced the Your First Home scheme in September and is expected to confirm further details when Chancellor John Healey delivers his Budget on Wednesday.

Under the proposals, eligible first-time buyers in England would be able to access a government-backed equity loan worth 20% of a new-build home's value.

The loans would be subject to an initial interest-free period and are intended to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.

Households earning less than £110,000 would qualify, while the threshold would be £140,000 for homes bought in London.

The scheme is similar to previous programmes including Help to Buy, which also used equity loans to support home purchases.

Unveiling it at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".

Previous schemes did not restrict eligibility by income, but faced criticism from some who argued they helped push up house prices by allowing wealthier households to borrow more.

Anstee said he would be hesitant to take on additional borrowing.

"I don't want to add more loans," he said.

"That is still a loan. [The government] do not specify how long it's interest-free for.

"You may save that initially, but once that interest starts kicking in on that loan, it could come back to kick you in the backside.

"I think it would help people get onto the property ladder but, in the long run, it is not a good idea.

"It feels like a bit of a gamble because you are relying on interest rates in the future to be stable."

Julia Weston, from Wellington, has worked as an estate agent for more than 30 years.

She said it was difficult to know whether a scheme like this would succeed.

"If you were to take out what is effectively a shared equity loan like Help to Buy was and then interest rates go up, you have got to fold in a massive chunk of money at your five-year mortgage renewal at a higher interest rate," she said.

"What if you lose your job, what if you have an unexpected baby or you lose one of your wage incomes?

"You are not just getting that share - you've got to remember that on the share that you rent from whatever organisation it is."

articles.title: Alexander brothers, ex-luxury real estate brokers, to be sentenced on federal sex trafficking charges
articles.summary: Federal prosecutors are seeking life sentences for Oren, Alon and Tal Alexander.
articles.body: Two former luxury real estate brokers and their brother are scheduled to be sentenced in a New York City courtroom Tuesday, seven months after they were convicted of drugging and raping women in a sex trafficking ring. Federal prosecutors are seeking life sentences for Oren and Alon Alexander, a pair of former powerful real estate brokers, and their brother, Tal. Attorneys for the brothers, who have asserted their innocence, are seeking 15-year sentences for each defendant. The men were found guilty in March of 10 counts, including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking and sex trafficking by force, after a trial that included testimony from 11 women who described being lured, drugged and sexually assaulted over a period of years. Six of the women were part of the indictment. In a sentencing memo, prosecutors in New York’s Southern District said more than 70 women came forward with allegations of abuse and accused the brothers of exploiting their wealth, influence and connections to target victims. At trial, prosecutors said the brothers raped the women after having promised them parties and trips. One woman testified that she lost control of her body after she had a drink with Alon Alexander at a New York City club. When she awoke, she testified, they were naked on a bed. She kept trying to get up, and he kept pushing her back down, she said. When she told him that she didn’t want to have sex with him, she testified, he responded, “‘You already did.’” In a sentencing submission, attorneys for the brothers acknowledged that they sometimes behaved insensitively toward women but categorically denied that any of them had raped or sexually assaulted anyone. At trial, the attorneys described the sex as consensual and said the women were motivated in part by financial gain. “All the stories were rehearsed,” Tal Alexander’s attorney, Deanna Paul, said in her closing argument. “They’re looking for money.”

articles.title: RAF Cosford museum looks for volunteers to pack up collection
articles.summary: The RAF Museum at Cosford is preparing to transfer over 50,000 items from a base in Stafford.
articles.body:
An RAF museum is looking for more volunteers to help it catalogue and pack items in its collection, ahead of a big move.

More than 50,000 objects are due to be transferred to the Royal Air Force Museum at Cosford, from an MoD storage facility in Stafford.

They will go on display in a new permanent exhibition at the Shropshire museum in 2028, a year later than originally planned.

The museum's Collections Care and Conservation Manager, Amy Seadon, said the items in Stafford dated from "the early days of flight, to the modern day".

She added: "We have everything from the very tiniest pin badge, all the way up to full aeroplanes such as Spitfire."

The packing and cataloguing began with the larger items and has gradually moved down to smaller and smaller objects.

She said getting the items out of storage and out on display would be "transformational".

"At the moment it feels very hidden away, but when we are at Cosford in a brand new hub, then any visitor will be able to come and see this and interact with these items," she said.

The collection is made up of items donated by individuals with a connection to the RAF and from the air force itself.

She added: "I'm constantly finding interesting objects."

Packing up the collection for the move will take thousands of hours, and Seadon explained that the volunteers would be involved in almost every step of the process.

Almost every item needs to be cleaned before being carefully packed and she said it was a bit like a house move, but "a lot more complicated and with more packing materials".

Volunteers are given the training and tools to complete their tasks, but do not need a background in museum work.

Seadon added: "You just need to have practical skills and also just be interested in the museum and the objects, you don't have to have any special knowledge."

"Just have an interest and be willing," she said.

Volunteering opportunities can be found on the RAF Museum Midlands website and she added: "The more the merrier, because we have a lot to move."

articles.title: Leaders of Norway, Finland hold rare call with Putin in break with previous European stance
articles.summary: The leaders of Finland and Norway called Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday to urge him to end the war in Ukraine, breaking with a longstanding practice among Western European leaders of shunning direct contact with the Kremlin.
articles.body: The leaders of Finland and Norway called Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday to urge him to end the war in Ukraine, breaking with a longstanding practice among Western European leaders of shunning direct contact with the Kremlin. The phone call by Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere was a bid to influence the diplomatic process at a time when President Donald Trump has shifted his position in favor of Russia and U.S. ties with Ukraine have hit their lowest point in 18 months. The Nordic leaders spoke by phone to Putin and afterward to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, according to a Zelenskyy aide. “The discussion (with Putin) was frank and substantive. We are neighboring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions,” Stubb said in a joint statement with Stoere. The Norwegian added: “The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations. In the call we stressed the importance of de-escalation.” Both leaders stressed their strong support for Ukraine, which they said would continue. The Kremlin’s readout of the call did not suggest that Putin had signaled any compromise from previously stated positions. “It was emphasized that achieving a just and long-term peace is possible only if the legitimate interests of the Russian Federation are fully and unconditionally taken into account,” the Kremlin said. “At the same time, attention was drawn to the confrontational policies of EU and NATO countries, which are contributing to the prolongation of the hostilities.” Western European leaders have mostly shunned contact with Putin, while piling up sanctions on Moscow, since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. But that stance has left them sidelined as efforts to end the war have been led by Trump, who is seen in many EU capitals as unpredictable, erratic and prone to side with Putin at the expense of Ukraine. That perception has been reinforced by deals this month in which Putin agreed to supply Russian diesel to the US and Trump eased sanctions on Russia while saying it was time for Ukrainians to replace Zelenskyy as their leader. Ukraine has also complained of disruption to intelligence-sharing by the US and to satellite internet services on which its military relies. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticized the Finnish-Norwegian decision to talk to Putin, adding that she saw no signs that Russia wants peace. “I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo,” Frederiksen told public broadcaster DR. Stubb and Stoere participated in the call as leaders of their respective countries and did not speak on behalf of Europe as a whole, they said, adding that the two Nordic nations will continue their longstanding support for Ukraine. Russia has frequently accused European governments of stoking the war by arming Ukraine and refusing direct talks. It has contrasted the stance of Western European leaders with that of Trump, who has engaged with Putin and tried — so far without success — to broker a peace agreement.

articles.title: New Hampshire journalist says he was blocked from covering Kamala Harris political event
articles.summary: Reporter Leonard Robinson claimed New Hampshire Democrats and Chris Pappas' staff blocked him from accessing an event with former Vice President Kamala Harris.
articles.body: A New Hampshire journalist said he was denied entry to an event Saturday featuring former Vice President Kamala Harris. "The reception that I've gotten at past Democrat events from activists, from staff has mostly been positive… which is what makes this situation so disappointing," New Hampshire Journal reporter Leonard Robinson told Fox News Digital in an interview Monday. Robinson wrote on X Saturday, "@NHDems often make access hard for NHJournal. I've been physically blocked by their operatives, they've hidden locations of their events from NHJournal. Nothing compares to Harris's visit." Harris was on the campaign stump in the Granite State for Democratic New Hampshire Senate candidate Chris Pappas. DEM HANDLERS LASH OUT WHEN CAMERAMAN CONFRONTS THEIR BOSS ABOUT DEBATE: ‘NO PICTURES’ Robinson said he RSVP'd to an event hosted by Reproductive Freedom for All (RFA) by filling out a form sent to him by the Pappas campaign after being shut out of another Harris event hosted by the campaign itself due to spatial constraints, according to an email obtained by Fox News Digital. When he arrived to check in, Robinson said a representative of RFA told him he wasn't on the registration list and said the event was at full capacity. Robinson said another journalist who was not on the list was later allowed inside. He also said he saw a Pappas campaign staffer gesture "no" to the RFA representative from a distance. FEDERAL JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TO RESTORE WHITE HOUSE ACCESS TO CNN, MS NOW AND POLITICO Robinson told Fox News Digital he had attended other Pappas campaign events featuring prominent Democrats, including California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Sen. Raphael Warnock of Georgia. "Why are [New Hampshire Democrats] afraid for her to talk to me? I think that's the real question that's gotta be answered here," Robinson said. KAMALA HARRIS FACES DEMOCRATIC DOUBTS OVER 2028 AS ALLIES PUSH BACK ON CLAIMS SHE’S SQUANDERED HER CHANCE Robinson, whose outlet New Hampshire Journal is among the state's only right-of-center publications, has had cordial in-person interactions with Pappas staff in the past but expressed frustration at the lack of cooperation from New Hampshire Democrats broadly in sharing its event calendar and being more welcoming to the outlet. New Hampshire Democratic Party Chair Raymond Buckley criticized New Hampshire Journal, calling the outlet "a partisan right wing site created to smear Democrats" and saying it "has rarely, if ever, received credentials to any Democratic or progressive event" in response to Robinson's X thread. NH Journal managing editor Michael Graham stood by Robinson, telling Fox News Digital, "This is a rare occasion for them to literally force Leonard out of, or one of us out of the event. And given Vice President Kamala Harris and her potential hopes to make history, it was really unfortunate that they would keep [out] a reporter from an award-winning member of the New Hampshire Press Association." It is unclear whether a miscommunication error among the Democratic organizers was behind the incident. Neither representatives for Harris nor the New Hampshire Democratic Party responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. A spokesperson for the Pappas campaign declined to comment. Harris has taken part in several campaigns for Democratic candidates ahead of the midterm elections. Her appearances also come as she weighs a potential 2028 presidential bid. articles.summary: Alan Dysert, the actor best known for his role in the television drama “All My Children,” has died, his wife said in a statement.
articles.body: Alan Dysert, the actor best known for his role in the television drama “All My Children,” has died, his wife said in a statement. He was 75 when he died on Friday. “My heart is broken as I share that my beloved husband, Alan, passed away,” Michelle Dysert said in a Facebook post on her husband’s page. She added that, “While I am struggling to imagine life without him, I am forever grateful to have experienced what so many people spend their lives searching for — the love of a lifetime.” His cause of death was not immediately clear. Dysert previously wrote about his long-running battle with cancer in a 2023 memoir: “Lights, Camera, Cancer!” According to Michelle Dysert’s post, her husband “faced more than his share of health challenges over the years,” but she did not detail what those health challenges were. “He continued to approach life with determination, humor, and gratitude,” she added. “He fought hard for the life he loved, and I was honored to stand beside him through it all.” In the Facebook post, Michelle Dysert described her husband’s “extraordinary life,” calling him “my partner, and my best friend.” “From his humble beginnings as a farm boy in Illinois, he went on to become an actor, musician, writer, filmmaker, producer, and beloved acting teacher,” she wrote. “Many knew him from his years on All My Children, while thousands of others knew him as the teacher and mentor who encouraged them to believe in themselves and pursue their dreams.” Dysert played the devious yet humorous conman Sean Cudahy on ABC’s “All My Children” soap opera non-consecutively from 1980-1990. According to his IMDb page, Dysert appeared in 79 episodes. He also appeared in the family comedy “Two Weeks” with actor Sally Field in 2006 and his most recent acting role was this year in the civil war movie, “The Legend of Van Dorn,” according to IMDb. In recent years, Dysert mentored upcoming actors and professional speakers and was passionate in helping them to overcome their fears of speaking and performing in public. Michelle Dysert hailed her husband’s “incredible gift for storytelling, a wonderful sense of humor, an adventurous spirit, and a personality that could fill any room. His life was filled with remarkable experiences, fascinating people, and enough stories for several lifetimes.” “Even after all our years together, life with Alan was never boring,” Michelle Dysert wrote. His wife said that in his book, Dysert had wanted his family to celebrate his life rather than mourn his passing. He “understood that life was an adventure, that tomorrow was never guaranteed, and that the greatest treasures weren’t things, but the people and experiences that made life meaningful,” she said.

articles.title: Watch: Serbia protesters storm pro-Aleksandar Vucic TV newsroom, capture editor
articles.summary: Protesters entered the newsroom of Serbian broadcaster Informer TV on Monday evening, interrupting its coverage and demanding the arrest of its
articles.body: Protesters entered the newsroom of Serbian broadcaster Informer TV on Monday evening, interrupting its coverage and demanding the arrest of its editor-in-chief, Dragan Vucicevic.The incident came as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for a second night to celebrate the election victory of the student-led Student List, which ended former President Aleksandar Vucic's 14-year hold on power.Live footage from Informer TV showed around 30 protesters entering the newsroom and gathering around Vucicevic. Some shouted, "This is how it is in free Serbia" and "Where is Vucic now?" while others called for the editor's arrest.Vucic, who previously served as information minister under former Serbian leader Slobodan Milosevic, maintained a strong grip on the country's media during his years in power.In a post on his personal Instagram account, Vucic condemned the incident as an attack on free speech and press freedom. He was pictured wearing a jumper bearing the crossed-out word "sorry".Student movement urges supporters to remain calmThe Student List emerged from a student-led anti-corruption movement and secured a historic election victory on Sunday, ending Vucic's 14 years in power.However, the movement has no clearly established leader, leaving questions over who will become prime minister and take up other senior government positions.Cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, the leading candidate on the Student List's election slate, appealed to supporters to remain peaceful while the electoral process continued."We ask of you to stay calm and dignified until the end of the electoral process, just like you have been until now," he said in a video posted on his Instagram account. "Don’t resort to any form of violence. Your Student List and your student movement urge you on this."Meanwhile, the Independent Association of Journalists of Serbia said it would submit an application on Tuesday seeking the withdrawal of Informer TV's broadcasting licence. The association cited what it described as systematic violations of the law and the broadcaster's programming obligations.Vucicevic accused the incoming political movement of seeking to silence media outlets critical of it."On the very first day of (Student List) power, they want to ban the media. They have said everything about themselves, and nothing about us," he told Reuters.Another group of protesters gathered outside Pink TV, a privately owned broadcaster supportive of Vucic, in Belgrade on Monday evening. Police cordoned off the building.State broadcaster apologises Separately, public broadcaster RTV in Serbia's northern Vojvodina region began its evening news bulletin with an apology to viewers, acknowledging that it had failed to fulfil its role through uncritical and one-sided reporting.The move echoed an incident in Hungary in July, when the country's main state television channel displayed a black screen carrying the message, "Public media cannot lie. We apologise for doing so for many years." This followed the election defeat of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban's Fidesz party three months earlier.Serbia has faced sustained criticism over media freedom and the uneven treatment of political opponents on television.The country ranked 104th among 180 nations in Reporters Without Borders' 2026 World Press Freedom Index, its lowest position to date and the worst in the EU-Balkan region.Election monitoring organisation Crta reported last week that television channels with nationwide reach devoted three-quarters of the airtime allocated to politicians to government representatives.Crta also found that the Student List was portrayed negatively in more than 80% of the instances in which it was discussed.The protests and the calls for changes to broadcasting practices have placed Serbia's media landscape under fresh scrutiny following the election result. The response of the incoming political leadership, including how it handles broadcasters supportive of the former government, is likely to be closely watched as the country moves towards forming a new administration.You use AI every day.
